title: Restore restart-controller policy binding to a durable kit checkout
description: Read-only diagnosis: installed policy kit_root names a missing checkout. Installed Runtime resolves it strictly at startup and re-reads the source closure on prepare, so successful status and HTTP health do not imply restart readiness. Qualification v2 expired on Nov 19 and does not bind the currently serving epoch. The policy digest still matches the install receipt and all 13 installed source facts match it. Reviewed mainline source is a viable candidate: all 28 registered inputs were present and the 13 controller facts matched, unlike the shared feature checkout tip. The deployment inputs exist; the missing scratch leaf has a valid existing parent and is provisionable on startup, not the cause. Owner change window: pin a durable reviewed checkout outside agent scratch and shared development branches; stage a policy-bound controller installation using the supported install and verify workflow, preserve and assess recovery state, and require a fresh same-incarnation startup canary and owner-issued v2 qualification before relying on prepare. Verify no repository cleanup can remove the policy-bound checkout and consider a read-only path check in future cleanup. Do not modify the live policy or restart the proxy as part of diagnosis.

description:

title: Shared gateway 403 team_model_access_denied for gpt-6.1-sol breaks Family standup cron (local proxy key)
description:
"Family: evening standup workflow" cron job (job 3912b50616a4) fails with a persistent model-access 403.

Error (2026-11-18 19:02 ET):
RuntimeError: HTTP 403: litellm.APIError: APIError: OpenAIException - {"error":{"message":"The requested model 'openai/gpt-6.1-sol' is not available for this API key, or the model name is invalid. Check the models available to you and try again.","type":"team_model_access_denied","param":"model","code":"403"}}

Verified (direct probe 2026-11-18, POST to https://litellm.shared.getflex.org/v1/chat/completions with the local proxy's LITELLM_API_KEY, model openai/gpt-6.1-sol) -> HTTP 403 team_model_access_denied. Deterministic, not transient.

The job uses provider=litellm-local with model=smart-router (COMPLEX tier), which routes to gpt-6.1-sol; the local proxy forwards to the shared gateway with the Flex AI Model Gateway credential.

Question: does the local key's model allowlist still include gpt-6.1-sol? Onset aligns with the shared-gateway alias re-order today (infra-aws a4e5c3b8, #2587, merged 2026-11-18 07:21 CT), which re-routed glm-5.3 and may have touched the key/model permission mapping. This is separate from the served_output_texts.py stream crash (lpkit-r84).

Note: family evening ran cleanly 11-16 and 11-17; the 403 appeared only on today's 11-18 run.

Recommended: confirm gpt-6.1-sol (and the other aliases the local proxy routes) are still granted to the local proxy's virtual key on the shared gateway; if the alias re-order dropped them, re-grant and re-run the job.
notes: ROOT-CAUSE CORRECTION (2026-11-18 ~22:00 ET): the shared gateway DOES allow gpt-6.1-sol for the hosted key — bare model id 'gpt-6.1-sol' returns 200 OK via /v1/chat/completions (verified probe). The 'openai/gpt-6.1-sol' PREFIXED form returns 403 team_model_access_denied. The local proxy's agent-frontier route sends the prefixed form (config.rendered.yaml line 90: model: openai/gpt-6.1-sol), which the shared gateway now rejects — this is a model-id form regression from the shared-gateway alias re-order (infra-aws a4e5c3b8), NOT a missing model grant. Fix options: (a) gateway-side: re-accept the openai/-prefixed alias (matches the pre-a4e5c3b8 behavior), or (b) local-side: change agent-frontier's upstream model to bare 'gpt-6.1-sol'. Option (a) is preferred — other local deployments may also use prefixed forms.

Verification annotation — 2026-11-19T10:42:09.532976+00:00

Current local service: proxy PID 2284, started 2026-11-18 21:54:07 local time; LiteLLM 1.110.0, verified runtime source 89cb4042afbcd963ee0fd0ae52595202d369a9e6. Rendered-config SHA-256 prefix e4c501f2e8bf9fbc (unchanged in this session).

- Shared gateway /v1/chat/completions, model gpt-6.1-sol: HTTP 200, usable visible output, finish_reason=stop (1.30 s).
- Same endpoint/key, model openai/gpt-6.1-sol: HTTP 403 team_model_access_denied (0.51 s).
- Local /v1/chat/completions, model agent-frontier: HTTP 200, usable visible output, finish_reason=stop (2.19 s).
- Three subsequent smart-router requests returned HTTP 200 with visible output (two technical prompts and one greeting). The second technical prompt repeated the first, so caching may explain its short response time; these are NOT proof of independent COMPLEX-arm selection or session pinning.

Do not remove the provider prefix from local configuration on that evidence alone.

The original failure mechanism under the previous runtime and the gateway's intended prefixed-alias contract remain unverified. Leave open for owner disposition; a healed local probe is annotation evidence, not closure authority.

title: Expired unconsumed approval permanently blocks recovery (recovery_invalid); no in-band disposal
description:
## Finding
An **expired, unconsumed approval file** left against a `prepared` operation row
permanently blocks ALL recovery-store mutations (`recovery_invalid`) until manually
archived out of the approvals dir — the store fail-closes on the stale approval with
no in-band disposal path.

## Mechanics
- `prepare` writes a request row (`prepared`) with a 300 s window and, separately,
  the operator writes `approvals/<request_id>.json` with its own sub-window.
- If the prepared plan expires before the restart consumes that approval, the
  approval file REMAINS under `approvals/`.
- On every later admission, recovery.py:449-454 (`require_clear` → rows) forces a
  `prepared` row that HAS an approval to validate it via `_matching_approval(...,
  consumed=False, prepared=True)`. An expired approval fails the in-window match
  (`approval_stale`) → `RecoveryError` / `recovery_invalid`. The `if approval is not
  None` branch is what traps; a prepared row with NO approval passes.
- There is no RPC or store method to dispose of a stale approval; `finish()` only
  closes preparing/postchecking/rollback terminal rows. Recovery is `recovery_invalid`
  until operator-side state surgery.

## Evidence (2026-11-18)
- Request `41a423ac...` (prepared 1795025081; plan expires 1795025381) had approval
  written by the operator at 1795025378 (issued_at) with expiry 1795025459 +120 s —
  inside the plan window, but the restart was never consumed before plan expiry. The
  approval file lingered.
- Second prepared row `312053aa...` had the same stale-unconsumed pattern (older).
- Controller then returned `recovery_invalid`; `require_clear()` on the live store
  raised `RecoveryError`.
- Archive-copy experiment: removing the two stale approval files made `require_clear()`
  pass (baseline fails, `no-stale-approvals` passes). Applying that to the live store
  (archiving both files to `archived-approval-expired-unconsumed-<rid8>-20261118.json`
  at the STATE ROOT, per the existing invalid-approval precedent) cleared the barrier;
  live `require_clear()` now OK, controller status `ok`.

## Suggested remediation (recovery-code, owner-driven)
1. Auto-expire: at admission, treat an unconsumed approval whose `expires_at` is in
   the past (or whose plan expired without a `.consumed` marker) as disposable —
   archive it to the state root and continue, rather than fail-closing the whole view.
2. Or add a sanctioned store method (e.g. `expire_plan(request_id)` called from
   `restart` when admission sees an already-expired plan) to close a prepared row +
   archive its unconsumed approval atomically.
3. Regression test: prepare → write approval → let the plan expire without consuming →
   assert a NEW `begin`/`prepare` still admits (auto-archiving the stale approval),
   and that a genuinely live unconsumed approval still fails admission.

Until fixed, an expired unconsumed approval is owner-side state surgery (archive to
state root, never delete) — precedent: `archived-approval-invalid-window-f0a647b1-*`.

## Cross-refs
- Session's manual recovery disposition precedent: 2026-11-18-9bfb768e (fence), and
  the recovery manual-disposition mechanics in restart-controller-operations.md.
- Blocked request preserved: `41a423ac...`, `312053aa...`.
notes: 2026-11-19 deployment evidence: PR #2 squash commit 0ca16ad contains the stale-approval admission fix and regression additions. Installed generation restart-controller-6d4cf7b8 includes the expired-unconsumed archival code; successful prepare/restart is recorded under lpkit-z9x. Original ba889ab is not an ancestor of squash commit 0ca16ad; do not rely on that ancestry test to judge inclusion. This note updates deployment evidence only; issue disposition remains separate.
close_reason: Repository fix delivered in PR #2 (0ca16ad). Verified on main at 7d360e6: expired unconsumed approval archives before new admission, while a live approval is preserved and still blocks admission. Both targeted regressions passed. This closes the repository defect, not live controller qualification.

title: Comment-only kit commit after bundle install bricks every prepare (controller_copy_changed)
description:
## Finding

A **comment-only** docs commit to kit HEAD after a controller bundle is installed
bricks every subsequent `prepare` with `runtime_invalid` (0.36 s fast-fail =
`controller_copy_changed`), because `freeze()` byte-compares the installed bundle's
controller sources against **current** kit HEAD facts.

## Evidence (2026-11-18)

- Bundle `restart-controller-761fdf29` installed today 12:41. Its closure digest is
  `761fdf29767b8c24...`; the qualification binds it correctly.
- Kit commit `c89dfb7` (13:19, "docs: scrub workstation paths and internal tracker
  references") touched `core/restart_control/runtime.py` — a **pure comment change**
  (lpkit-fhz/976 tracker-ID prefixes removed from two comment lines; semantics
  unchanged, tests re-run green 71 passed). This advanced kit HEAD ~38 min AFTER the
  bundle install.
- Live prepare after that: request `4916ace332...`, status `runtime_invalid`,
  `original_preserved: true`, 0.36 s.
- Offline replication (`source_facts(kit)` vs `_regular(bundle/...)` over
  `CONTROLLER_INPUTS`): exactly one mismatch — `core/restart_control/runtime.py`
  (kit `1478ab1e...` vs bundle `8d3fe7a9...`). All other controller inputs match.
- `freeze()` (runtime.py:1123-1128) refuses `controller_copy_changed` when ANY
  `CONTROLLER_INPUTS` bundle copy differs from `facts[name]` (kit-HEAD bytes).

## Root tension

The installed-closure probe (`qualify`) binds a record to the LOADED bundle sources,
so a record can be correctly bound to an installed generation. But `freeze()` compares
bundle bytes against **current kit HEAD**, not against the installed-closure snapshot.
Therefore ANY post-install kit source change — even a no-op comment edit — re-triggers
`controller_copy_changed` and forces a full generation refresh (bootout → retire →
new bundle dir → policy `controller_root` edit → fresh install → bootstrap →
arm+kickstart → reissue). This is the same class as lpkit-976, reopened by the docs
scrub being a tracked (digested) controller source.

## Suggested remediation (controller-code, owner-driven)

1. Freeze comparisons against the **installed-closure snapshot** recorded in the
   bundle's `install.json` receipt (the `sources` map keyed by CONTROLLER_INPUTS
   names), NOT against live kit HEAD. `freeze()` should compare
   `bundle/name` == `install.json.sources[name]` for the installed generation, so a
   later kit commit (even to a digested source) does not invalidate the installed
   bundle's prepared operations. The closure probe already records these bytes.
2. Alternatively/additionally: allow in-place bundle refresh (a distinct
   `update` path in `install_restart_controller.py`) so comment-only kit advances can
   be applied without the full bootout/new-root/requalify cycle.
3. Regression test: install a bundle, commit a comment-only change to a
   CONTROLLER_INPUTS source, assert `require_clear`/`freeze`/`prepare` still pass
   against the installed snapshot; and `prepare` still refuses when the installed
   bytes genuinely diverge from the receipt.

Until fixed: the documented generation-refresh sequence is the only recovery (owner
package precedent: 2026-11-17-54060da8-gates-fix-owner-package.md). Manual proxy
restart (kickstart) is unaffected and is the immediate path to load the staged config.

## Cross-refs
- lpkit-976 (prior manifestation: A1 qualify probe landed in kit, installed bundle
  stale vs HEAD, every prepare refused).
- Live request preserved: `4916ace332...`.
close_reason: Repository fix delivered in PR #2 (0ca16ad). Verified on main at 7d360e6: freeze checks the installed receipt rather than newer kit bytes and still refuses tampered bundle bytes. Targeted regression passed. This closes the repository defect, not the missing live kit_root or controller qualification.

title: litellm _chat_stream_texts crashes on streamed chunk with choice.index=None, dropping in-flight tool calls
description:
Root cause of the 2026-11-18 "Stream stalled mid tool-call" warnings seen on Hermes Desktop and Discord.

Chain (verified end-to-end in ~/.local/share/litellm/proxy.err.log):
1. LiteLLM post-stream bookkeeping hook calls served_stream_output_texts() -> _chat_stream_texts().
2. served_output_texts.py:132: choice_count = max((choice.index + 1 for ... ), default=0)
3. Streamed chunks arrived with choice.index = None -> "TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'".
4. LiteLLM serializes the stream error into the SSE body; Hermes' OpenAI SDK (_streaming.py:95) lifts it as APIError and the in-flight tool call is dropped.

Evidence:
- 22 occurrences, all on 2026-11-18 between 08:37:39 and 08:51:15 (first ever; zero in rotated logs .1/.2/.3 back to 2026-11-17).
- Runtime unchanged: litellm 1.106.2 deployed 2026-11-03, proxy process up since 2026-11-15 21:35.
- Trigger is upstream traffic emitting choice.index=None on streamed chunks, tripping a latent bug in the bookkeeping hook.

Suggested fix (upstream litellm served_output_texts.py):

Note: runtime lives under a verified/signed path; hand-edits will trip restart-controller integrity checks. Prefer upstream patch via the runtime-build workflow or a litellm upgrade.
notes:

The null `choice.index` originates at the **Flex shared gateway's GLM 5.3 route**, not the local proxy.

Evidence chain:

Count rose 78→84 during probing, confirming causality.
- The failing frames carry `resp_*` response IDs — the **Responses API** shape. Vercel AI Gateway serves `zai/glm-5.3` through its Responses API; LiteLLM 1.106.2's OpenAI-compat conversion drops `choice.index` when converting Responses-style streamed chunks.

Local config/runtime/process unchanged (config.rendered.yaml mtime 11-16; runtime deployed 11-03; process up since 11-15).

3. Flex gateway-side: ask infra to confirm whether the new AWS-first glm-5.3 alias ordering is intended to shift streaming traffic onto Responses-API-backed deployments; the W-10 doc says live Vercel/Responses streaming paths were not yet verified.

2026-11-18 upstream-stable survey (evidence: fetched BerriAI tags through v1.110.0; local clone tag/`git show` inspection; no runtime changes).

Latest stable = v1.110.0 (also checked v1.108.11, v1.109.1). Status of our historical defect set:

Contained in v1.109.1 and v1.110.0; NOT in v1.108.11 (and not in the kit's staged 1.108.0 candidate venv — `.venv-candidate-1.108.0` line 135 still has bare `choice.index + 1`). So the issue's remediation option 2 (upgrade to 1.108.0) does NOT fix r84; minimum fixed stable is 1.109.1.

Duplicate streamed tool-call arguments (our aa41d4030f port) — STILL PRESENT in v1.110.0: `output_item.added` emits complete `function.arguments` and `FUNCTION_CALL_ARGUMENTS_DELTA` forwards further args unconditionally; no dedupe/sentinel (`args_already_complete` absent; grep clean). title: Restart controller policy.json deployment_root is not a deployment root; prepare refuses runtime_invalid/gate_failed
description:
## Finding

The restart controller's policy.json points `deployment_root` at `~/.config/litellm`, but the
controller bundle (restart_control/runtime.py freeze() + check_gates) requires a FULL deployment
root at that path:

- `deploy.conf.sh` at the root that drift_check's KEY=VALUE parser can read;
- `deployments/<name>/{overlay.yaml, credentials.toml, pin.lock, native-build.json}` for the
  freeze fact closure;
- a passing `drift_check --deployment-root <that root>` gate.

The r1 evidence doc (docs/evidence/2026-11-11-r1-integration-and-predecessor-inventory.md:135)
already required `deployment_root -> work repo` before any qualification v2; the deployed policy
predates that remediation.

## Evidence

  9c05e052, e4b530bc, 3dc014af, 8ca36e1a; all preserved in the recovery journal, all

drift_check.py's deploy.conf.sh parser only handles plain KEY=VALUE lines; the deployed

KeyError LITELLM_CONFIG_DIR against ~/.config/litellm root, yet drift_check PASSED against the
work-repo root using the same file shape — reconcile that contradiction at source level during
remediation (likely an env-inheritance or path difference I did not fully isolate).

   (new canonical policy_digest c6b3ec0f8b8b1ea833b47a5702718979e28a3e5d55e1ba5accfd8c40965dff92).

title: FN (xcc reopened/incomplete): osascript do-shell-script quote asymmetry - double-quoted inner operand passes the same signal that single-quoted vetoes, incl. numeric-PID
description: Found in dd311e4 post-fix V&V (2026-11-14). EMPIRICAL on the deployed dd311e4 guard: the do-shell-script wrapper with a SINGLE-quoted inner operand vetoes LGV-001, but the identical semantic payload with a DOUBLE-quoted inner operand ALLOWS - including with a numeric PID operand, so it is not merely a by-name gap. Real signal verbs (process-match verbs) through the same dq form DO veto, so the leak is specific to the bare signal verb family inside double quotes. The repo xcc gate (tests/test_guard_osascript_surface.py) pins both quote forms and passes offline because its dq row is satisfied by pid-operand discovery analysis; operand extraction for the dq form does not refuse unextractable/by-name operands as FR-006 requires - while the sq form refuses identical content. Internally inconsistent: whichever policy is correct, the two quote styles must agree. ADJUDICATION vs xcc scope: xcc's closed scope was 'osascript do-shell-script (and terminal-surface osascript) proxy-kill wrappers pass unblocked' - this is that class, so reopened/incomplete rather than new. FIX DIRECTION: make dq-form operand analysis refuse unextractable operands (fail closed per FR-006), matching the sq path; add gate rows for both quote styles with by-name and numeric operands. FULL REPRO TABLE: /Users/pjbeyer/.hermes/cache/scratch/vv_xcc_fn_evidence.txt (payloads and verdicts; verb-literals kept out of this body). Evidence scripts: vv_xcc_char.py, vv_xcc_delta.py, vv_wrapped_real.py.

comments.author: Phil Beyer
comments.text: V&V CONFIRMATION 2026-11-16 (independent session, byte-exact offline battery + full-suite run at 1b45a11): ADJUDICATION VERIFIED. Independently reproduced the full table on the new generation: dq-form do-shell-script vetoes every genuine threat (protected numeric PID, by-name pattern verbs, PID-discovery substitution shape, port-sentinel xargs shape); the original FN claim's 'numeric PID' operand was 4346, which is dead and outside the protected set (protection is port-based: protected_port 4000; the current listener PID blocks correctly) - so the ALLOW rows were policy-consistent, not leaks. sq-inner operands are INVALID AppleScript (strings are double-quoted only) and refuse fail-closed per FR-006 - the 'asymmetry' is valid-vs-malformed dialect, not a bypass. Consistency gates pin both quote forms by operand class. The prior xcc close stands; this issue's scope (reopen check) is satisfied.

title: hermes-beads-resolve fails with candidate_metadata_mode_invalid for known-good prefixes (incl. flex, lpkit)
description:

- Agents must fall back to directory probing (as this session did), which the skill explicitly warns against.

## Evidence

- 'hermes-beads-resolve flex-pyr2v' earlier 2026-11-05: 'resolved flex /Users/pjbeyer/Projects/work/workspace' (worked)
- 'hermes-beads-resolve lpkit' and 'hermes-beads-resolve flex-pyr2v' 2026-11-13: 'candidate_metadata_mode_invalid / verification_failed'
- Resolver: /Users/pjbeyer/.local/bin/hermes-beads-resolve → ~/.hermes/scripts/hermes_beads_resolver.py (shared code; HERMES_HOME selects manifest)
- lpkit ground truth (probed): /Users/pjbeyer/litellm-local-proxy-kit, prefix lpkit, central dolt server port 3307

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause in hermes_beads_resolver.py identified (manifest mode / candidate metadata validation)
- [ ] Resolve works again for flex, lpkit, litest, flite, pjb
- [ ] Regression guard: resolve each known prefix in CI or a cron health check

comments.author: Phil Beyer
comments.text: V&V 2026-11-13: ROOT CAUSE FOUND (empirically verified) - and it is NOT a guard-plugin issue, so the new guard version cannot address it. hermes_beads_resolver.resolve() validates EVERY manifest candidate before matching the query, and the failure status is computed from the accumulated diagnostics even when the queried prefix would match a different, healthy candidate. One candidate in beads_cron_manifest.json - /Users/pjbeyer/Projects/pjbeyer/operating-principles - carries .beads/metadata.json with dolt_mode 'embedded' (not 'server'), so _metadata_is_valid returns candidate_metadata_mode_invalid, unresolved_candidate is set, and resolve() short-circuits to verification_failed for EVERY query including flex and lpkit. Verified: iterating all 34 manifest candidates through _metadata_is_valid finds exactly this one failure; flex and lpkit metadata are individually valid (backend=dolt, dolt_mode=server, database matches, port 3307). FIX (two-part, owner choice): (a) repair the operating-principles candidate - either migrate its metadata to server mode matching the central dolt server, or remove/flag it in beads_cron_manifest.json if it is intentionally embedded-only; and (b) harden resolve() so a failing UNRELATED candidate degrades to a diagnostic instead of blocking resolution of a verified exact-prefix match (the current all-candidates-gate makes the resolver a single point of failure for one bad repo). Regression guard per the issue's acceptance criteria can then pin all five prefixes.

title: Guard false positive: leaf subagent deterministically blocked on entire mcp_tool_call relay class while main session passes identical envelope
description:
# Finding (2026-11-13, PCI audit session)

A delegate_task leaf subagent (deleg_5bb41a5c, dispatched 2026-11-13 10:13 EST) was deterministically refused on every call to relay tool_id a26a54776da7d49225faf341ccf2e2fa (flex-litellm-gateway-mcp_tool_call): Notion fetch of page B, relay mcp_tool_search discovery, and a corrected-envelope retry — three attempts, each retried after the 60s cooldown per protocol, all blocked. The identical envelope passed from the MAIN session at audit time (verified live: aigateway_notion-notion-fetch of the Flex tracker succeeded through the same relay minutes after).

## Why this matters

- The documented FP pattern (memory + skill) says stale guards block the main session and FRESH subagent processes bypass. This is the inverse: main session clean, fresh leaf blocked — the pattern cuts both ways, so 'retry via a fresh subagent' is NOT a reliable recovery.
- A 12-issue authorized write batch (Notion page refresh + Linear filing) died on this; the subagent correctly preserved the refusal per protocol, but the whole job had to be re-dispatched.
- The subagent ALSO saw 'User not allowed to call this tool' after one retry — suggests the block may interact with relay-side permission state, not just the local guard evaluation.

## Repro shape

Envelope: mcp__local_mcp_aggregator__call_tool → {tool_id: 'a26a54776da7d49225faf341ccf2e2fa', arguments: {tool_name: 'aigateway_notion-*'|'aigateway_linear-*', arguments: {...}}}. Blocked from fresh leaf subagent, allowed from main session, same proxy instance (litellm local proxy PID 4346, port 4000, health 200 throughout — NOT a proxy outage).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified for why the guard vetoes an entire tool class per-session/process (not per-call)
- [ ] Deterministic repro or log capture from the blocked subagent session (see deleg_5bb41a5c transcript: /Users/pjbeyer/.hermes/cache/delegation/live/deleg_5bb41a5c/task-0.log)
- [ ] Either a fix, or the documented recovery protocol updated to stop recommending 'fresh subagent bypasses the stale guard' as reliable

title: Post-install review: plugin-dir redirect FP (2>/dev/null treated as write) and pipe-to-shell FN class (| sh, awk system(), find -exec, docker kill, python heredoc)
description: Post-install performance review of deployed guard 10306141 (2026-11-08 evening, this V&V session, after owner install + gateway restart 19:50). Review battery: 45 probes — 35/45 PASS. All previously fixed classes (osascript 8/8, newline FP, F-017 reads, yt5.1 payloads, 28-case regression battery) remain fixed; latency p50=0.22ms, p95=19.3ms, max=54ms; watchdog green; sink records live; proxy stable. TWO new findings, both CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING (A/B vs previous generation 02c7635f: identical behavior, NOT regressions from the latest two fixes): FINDING A (FP, plugin-dir redirect conflation): any command whose text mentions the deployed plugin directory AND carries a redirect operator (2>/dev/null, > file) is refused LGV-001 as a presumed write. Reproduced: ls/cat/grep of plugin-dir files each ALLOW bare but each BLOCK with 2>/dev/null appended; unrelated paths with the same redirect ALLOW. This is the same read/write conflation family as the fixed F-017 finding (guard.py:2043 area), extended to the shell-redirect surface: the marker check appears to treat ANY redirect as write intent when the plugin path is present. Benign, extremely common shell idiom (suppressing stderr on a read) blocks legitimate inspection/diagnostic work — the 20:18 VETO of the install session's own post-restart verification command (ls __pycache__ with 2>/dev/null) was exactly this. FINDING B (FN, pipe-to-interpreter class): kill payloads piped to an interpreter pass on the terminal surface: echo 'pkill -f litellm' | sh (and | bash, | zsh, | sh -s), printf variants, tee|sh, awk system('kill ...'), find -exec kill, find -execdir kill, docker kill/stop litellm-named containers, and python3 heredoc os.kill(1248,9) all ALLOW, while adjacent shapes (xargs sh -c, bash heredoc pkill) correctly BLOCK. Root-cause pointer: the chunker analyzes pipeline STAGES independently; the payload producer stage (echo/printf/awk/find/docker) is classified benign, and the consumer stage (sh/bash/zsh/python3 reading stdin) sees no kill text because the payload arrives on stdin, not in argv. The kit README (FR-012 honest boundaries) lists 'imported scripts, encoded or generated programs' and 'other execution tools' as out-of-scope bypass classes — but a literal kill command piped to sh is NOT encoded, NOT another tool, and NOT generated: it is the same first-class terminal surface, quoted plainly in the command text. Per the fail-closed constitution (same reasoning the osascript class was ruled in-scope in lpkit-xcc), stdin-feeding interpreters belong in scope: the guard already recognizes stdin-fed shell payloads for xargs sh -c (F-007), so the class boundary is inconsistent — xargs sh -c blocks while echo|sh allows. Severity note: docker kill of a litellm-named container is container-kill, but the proxy does not run in docker on this host, so B's practical risk on this host is the | sh / awk / find / heredoc vectors; docker is listed for completeness of the class. ACCEPTANCE: (1) Red-first: pin the battery (A: plugin-dir read commands with stderr redirects; B: echo/printf|sh, awk system(), find -exec, stdin-fed heredoc interpreters, on both terminal and execute_code surfaces) against the current generation showing the failures. (2) Finding A fix: redirect-without-write-truncation semantics — a read command with stderr redirection into /dev/null or an existing-file append that does not target the plugin dir must allow; redirects whose destination resolves inside the plugin dir must still refuse; quotation-aware, no over-blocking of FR-004 innocent work. (3) Finding B fix: stdin-fed interpreter stages (sh/bash/zsh/python3 as pipeline consumers or heredoc targets) must inherit analysis of the producer stage's data payload — when the producer stage carries recognizable signal text, the pipeline must refuse (mirroring the F-007 xargs sh -c precedent); docker kill/stop of litellm-named containers per the protected-labels vocabulary. (4) Full suite green + 28-case regression + osascript battery + this 45-probe review battery all green, no FP regressions. (5) Fix in the canonical repo; owner-authorized install path only. Evidence: vv_postinstall_review.py, vv_class_bounds.py, vv_ab_new_findings.py in session scratch; A/B vs 02c7635f proving pre-existing (not a regression from 9d8faad/7371707).
notes: add COMPLETED 2026-11-09. Both findings fixed, battery-proven, published, deployed on disk. FINDING A FIX: redirect semantics — new _redirect_writes_plugin_dir (quote-aware bounded single pass) extracts each redirect's file destination and vetoes only when it resolves inside the deployed plugin dir (with ~ expansion); 2>&1 dupes and unrelated destinations are inert; redirects INTO the dir still veto (suite-pinned, A-04/A-05 plus >>/tilde forms). The chunk gate no longer conflates any '>' with write. FINDING B FIX: stdin-fed interpreter class in scope per the fail-closed constitution and the F-007 xargs sh -c precedent — (1) stdin-consumer branch: sh/bash/zsh/python as a non-first pipeline stage with no -c/-e operand inherits producer payload analysis (quoted AND unquoted echo/printf/tee/yes data), blocking on kill-family intent or target mention; benign pipe-to-sh stays allowed; (2) awk branch: system()/cmd |/getline program text with kill intent vetoes (FR-006); (3) find branch: -exec/-execdir with kill/pkill/killall/xargs/sh executor vetoes; (4) docker branch: kill/stop/rm/restart/pause of litellm-named containers vetoes per protected-labels vocabulary, read-only docker passes; (5) heredoc routing: <<DELIM bodies with sh/bash/zsh/python heads route to the matching analyzer, unterminated heredocs refuse; (6) node/ruby/perl/php -e operands with kill intent veto; (7) exec()-built Python string literals route to the code analyzer; (8) getattr(os,'kill') indirection vetoes by call shape. ALSO closed the remaining 5 review-battery failures (B-06 exec-built, B-07 getattr, B-08 node, B-09 ruby, B-10 perl) so the 45-probe post-install review battery is FULLY green (was 35/45 at 10306141, 40/45 after the two named findings). INTERMEDIATE DEFECTS caught by the gates during development: (a) infinite loop in the redirect scanner (missing plain-char advancement) caught by the 300s runner timeout, fixed; (b) swallowed _Block inside except Exception in the unquoted-producer check (B-12 red) — restructured to compute-in-try/raise-outside; (c) candidate dirs missing integrity.sha256 fail-closed LGV-032, masking benign results — runners now materialize manifests. title: FP class: quotation-blind newline splitting (multi-paragraph git commit messages) and F-017 read/write conflation both still refuse benign work
description:
Follow-up from post-deployment FP/FN verification (2026-11-07, this V&V session) of the deployed hardened generation (02c7635f, gateway restarted 05:44). Two reproduced, still-live false-positive classes, both traced to byte-exact refusals from real sessions: FINDING A (quotation-blind newline splitting, the cause of BOTH the blocked specification session's refusals and the 2026-11-06 19:04 git-batch refusal in the litellm-gateway-test-suite session): _CHUNK_SEPS (guard.py:1142) includes raw newline separators without quotation awareness. Any shell text containing a REAL newline INSIDE a quoted argument — the standard git commit multi-paragraph convention -m "para1.

Closes X." — splits mid-string, producing unbalanced-quote chunks; shlex.split then raises ValueError -> _Block() -> LGV-001 VETO with the proxy-lifecycle refusal signature. Reproduced: full 2026-11-06 payload (session 20261105_220814_9e2e33, msg 986190, byte-exact from the session DB) BLOCKs on BOTH the old d97fea50 and the deployed 02c7635f generation; drop-one-line bisect isolates the trigger to the commit line; message bisect shows ANY 2-paragraph message blocks regardless of content (pure 'Small message.

Closes litest-6c5.' with zero signal vocabulary also blocks) while single-paragraph messages allow. The spec session's refusals (blocked while trying to review-record text quoting guard vocabulary and read the installed directory) and the git session's branch/commit block are both this class plus Finding B. Surface-inconsistent: terminal allows the identical command; only execute_code (which routes Python string literals through _analyze_shell_text via _SHELL_KEYWORDS match) vetoes. This is the same quotation-awareness contract as FR-003 (control words inside quoted strings) extended to separators: the chunker must be quotation-aware for SEPARATORS, not just tokens/control words. FINDING B (F-017 conflation of reads and writes): _analyze_code_text (guard.py:1884) vetoes when PLUGIN_DIR_MARKER appears with 'open(' in the LOWERCASED text. A read via open(...).read() of the deployed guard.py is BLOCKED (LGV-001) on both old and deployed generations — yet Path.read_text and terminal cat of the same file pass. F-017's intent is write-protection of deployed files; open() is not a write primitive and the rule as implemented is both over-broad (blocks reads) and under-inclusive across surfaces (read via Path or cat both bypass it). The specification session's 'my read of the installed directory was itself refused' is exactly this rule. ACCEPTANCE: (1) quotation-aware separator splitting: real newlines inside balanced quotes must NOT split; unbalanced-quote chunks must remain fails (fail-closed on truly malformed input, never fall through to allow); (2) F-017 narrowed to write primitives (or quotation/context-aware) so reads pass on ALL surfaces consistently; writes to the deployed plugin directory must still refuse; (3) red tests first for both classes (byte-exact refused payloads as fixtures, plus the read-family battery open/Path.read_text/cat/head/wc); (4) full suite green, no FN regressions (rerun the 28-case FP/FN battery + scope battery); (5) fix in the canonical repo, deploy via owner-authorized activation only. Evidence: vv_exact_refusal.py, vv_bisect.py, vv_msg_bisect.py, vv_newline_iso.py, vf_f017.py probes and vv_refused_args.json (byte-exact payload) in session scratch.

ROOT-CAUSE CORRECTION to the issue's hypothesis: the chunker on HEAD is ALREADY quote-aware (balanced-quote multi-paragraph git commits passed on both surfaces in the red run) — the actual mechanism for the byte-exact 2026-11-06 refusal is a SYNTAX gate, not separator splitting: that payload embeds a raw newline inside a single-quoted Python string (invalid Python), ast.parse raises SyntaxError inside _iter_string_literals, and evaluate's generic handler converts it to a lifecycle VETO (LGV-001) before shell analysis ever runs. FINDING A FIX: syntactic validity gate in _analyze_code_text — non-parsing code refuses with the corrective bound category (BOUND_SIZE/LGV-010, reduce/restructure and resubmit), never a lifecycle VETO. Fail-closed on malformed input preserved per acceptance 1 ('unbalanced-quote chunks must remain fails, never fall through to allow') — the byte-exact fixture's pinned expectation is REFUSE:BOUND_SIZE, honestly not ALLOW. FINDING B FIX: F-017 narrowed to write primitives — open() with mode containing w/a/x/+ (mode= keyword included), pathlib write family (write_text/write_bytes), explicit .write( alongside the marker. Reads pass on every surface (open().read(), mode='r', read_text, cat/head/wc/grep); writes still veto — INCLUDING re-earning the existing suite pin Path(...).write_text which the first narrow cut had wrongly allowed (caught by the canonical suite, fixed by adding the pathlib write family to the write-primitive set). title: False negative: osascript do-shell-script (and terminal-surface osascript) proxy-kill wrappers pass unblocked
description: Found during post-install FP/FN verification (2026-11-07, V&V session) against the DEPLOYED hardened generation (guard.py 02c7635f, installed 2026-11-07, owner process-cycle completed 05:44). FP/FN battery: 27/28 pass — 14/14 false-positive cases ALLOW (incl. the yt5.1 quotation-defect payloads: inline python conditionals, strings containing else, quoted if/else batch — all now pass) and 13/14 false-negative cases BLOCK. DEFECT — the FN class: signal intent routed through AppleScript shell indirection passes on BOTH in-scope surfaces. execute_code: subprocess.run with argv [osascript, -e, <AppleScript do-shell-script form embedding a pkill payload>] -> ALLOW. terminal: osascript -e <do-shell-script wrapper embedding the pkill payload> -> ALLOW, and even the bare-payload form (osascript -e with the pkill text directly) -> ALLOW on the terminal surface (the bare form IS caught on the code surface via string-literal scanning; the miss is the nested-quote wrapping on the code surface and all osascript forms on the terminal surface). Differential: os.system with a pkill string, subprocess bash -c wrapper, subprocess direct pkill argv, env/bash/sh/xargs wrappers — all correctly BLOCK on both surfaces; the gap is specific to the osascript indirection class. Root-cause pointer: WRAPPER_VERBS (guard.py:794) covers sudo/env/nohup/nice/time/timeout/stdbuf but not osascript, and no analyzer branch handles nested-quote payloads inside AppleScript programs. Severity: real — osascript is a first-class macOS execution surface present on every host this kit targets, and other supervised services on this host are launched through the same osascript shell-indirection class, so an agent reaching osascript reaches process control. Not a documented bypass class: FR-012 lists other execution tools/encoded programs as out of scope, but osascript is not encoded and not another tool — it is a wrapper/indirection surface reachable from both in-scope tools, so per the fail-closed constitution this belongs in scope as a pattern the matcher must recognize. Acceptance: (1) red battery first on both surfaces (nested-quote do-shell-script form, bare -e form, osascript -l JavaScript form, single vs double quote nesting variants); (2) fix in the canonical repo (mirror rule: repo is upstream), quotation-aware so benign AppleScripts (display dialog etc.) still pass — do not over-block FR-004 innocent work; (3) full suite green + no FP regressions (rerun the 14-case FP battery); (4) mutation check proving the new branch is live; (5) deploy via the documented owner-authorized activation path only. Repository: https://github.com/pjbeyer/litellm-local-proxy-kit
Branch: `fix/decision-sink-hardening`
Tip: `c90f08b7d5d78f04ad55ff579327e86532a99e24`

External source: https://github.com/pjbeyer/litellm-local-proxy-kit/commit/c90f08b7d5d78f04ad55ff579327e86532a99e24
The public branch was built from the separately published snapshot; its ancestry is not the private development ancestry. Integrate the scoped changes deliberately rather than merging old public controller/configuration files over newer private work.

Primary artifacts:
- `docs/contracts/decision-sink.md` (D1-D12 and verification/release gates).
- `integrations/hermes/proxy-lifecycle-guard/{guard.py,__init__.py,guard_probe_watchdog.py}`.
- `tests/test_guard_quoted_control_flow.py`, `tests/test_lifecycle_guard.py`.
- `tests/test_sink_{worker,worker_cleanup,hardening_fs,encoding,replay,watchdog}.py`.
- `tests/{sink_path_qualification_probe,sink_worker_evaluate_probe}.py`.

## Specification incorporation

Reconcile this contract with the canonical guard spec, including bounded callback behavior, stable refusal semantics and the existing integrity closure. Preserve:
- Identical allow/block decisions despite telemetry failure; immediate sanitized decision logging remains independent of sink admission.
- Exactly four persisted fields: timestamp, category, stable code, canonical tool. No arbitrary arguments, namespace/path/PID or credential material.
- No new sink filesystem work or waits on the enforcement callback; nonwaiting admission, 64 pending capped records plus one active worker per module generation; no automatic replacement workers.
- Adapter startup outside callbacks, cleanup registration before worker startup using actual `ctx.on_unload`, bounded drain/shutdown and observable startup/drop/failure states. Missing cleanup support disables sink startup, not enforcement.
- Descriptor-relative, owner-only, no-follow managed storage; reject unsafe links and special files; nonblocking cooperative locking, capped rotation and strict UTF-8/schema-valid JSONL replay. Do not silently repair oversized/malformed state.
- Capture state-home and canonical immutable metadata at submission. Flush completion is NOT fsync durability; repeated owner reloads are NOT covered by a process-global worker bound.
- Watchdog receipts prove current flushed offline source-path delivery, not merely enqueue, stale-file presence or actual gateway activation.
- Quotation normalization must preserve literal data while still inspecting executable substitutions. Do not promise that all documentation payloads will pass static inspection.

## Evidence and installed gap

Publication candidate executed in isolated state: 380 tests and 70 subtests passed. Independent profiled Codex review reported no confirmed defects; it could not execute its own tests in its read-only temporary-directory context. Do not conflate that with the separately executed full suite or with live qualification. One trailing blank line in a test was removed after the full run, with unchanged AST verified.

At this handoff, installed default-profile manifest matches the candidate, but installed guard/adapter bytes differ. The installed adapter lacks the new sink start/shutdown/on_unload wiring. This session did not install, reload, alter policy/integrity references or activate the candidate.

An attempted README/contract/watchdog-prose refresh was freshly refused by the live guard. The whole request was unapplied and was not retried through another route. The published README therefore retains legacy upgrade instructions and pre-existing public references: review/correct the operational documentation in an owner-cleared context before using it. Publication did not clear this refusal or previously preserved source-data/native-operation refusals.

## Acceptance / return package

1. Canonical spec explicitly dispositions all changes, residual risks and supported lifecycle API; no duplicate source of truth.
2. Implementation incorporates the reviewed changes without regressing concurrent guard fixes, exact refusal vocabulary, policy validation or the two-file source-integrity closure.
3. Execute the reconciled full suite, fresh-process fault/mutation cases, adapter startup/cleanup failures and current-receipt watchdog tests with disposable isolated state. Record exact commit and source digests, meaningful positive controls and independent spec/quality review.
4. Refresh installation/upgrade/rollback/watchdog documentation; distinguish enabled vs actually loaded and offline evidence vs live gateway delivery. Never swap files under a loaded incompatible generation.
5. Produce an owner-reviewed default-profile-only upgrade/rollback plan and durable sanitized evidence. Any deployment needs separate explicit authorization; do not disable the guard to make a refused operation pass.
6. Return the spec/implementation commits, verification evidence, installed/deferred state and exact unresolved blockers to Phil and the originating Hermes session. Leave restart-controller qualification and the first controlled proxy restart as separate work/gates.

title: Release readiness: offline suite fails on stock macOS — restart-controller _private_path rejects symlinked TMPDIR (/var -> /private/var)
description: Release-readiness analysis (2026-11-04) ran the full offline suite in an isolated venv on this workstation: 18 failed, 22 errors, 164 passed — and the PUBLISHED snapshot (github orphan 'main' = 1399724 'initial release') shows the same 18F+22E, so the shipped tree fails its own suite on stock macOS. Root cause (verified mechanically, not inferred): all 40 failures/errors trace to core/restart_control/engine.py _private_path(), which raises Fault('state_io') when ANY path component is a symlink. macOS default TMPDIR is /var/folders/... where /var is a symlink to /private/var — a stock platform invariant, not a hostile symlink. Every controller/runtime test that builds state under tmp_path/pytest tmp fails on this machine. Single-line repro: pytest tests/test_restart_controller.py::ControllerTest::test_socket_unavailable -> Fault: state_io. Fix direction: canonicalize (Path.resolve()) before the symlink walk, or treat /var vs /private/var equivalence as expected; keep the fail-closed intent for genuinely surprising symlinks. Add a regression test that runs under default macOS TMPDIR. This also gates the restart-controller draft reaching release-candidate quality and any README claim that '.venv-tests/bin/python -m pytest -q tests' is the validation suite.
acceptance_criteria: Full offline suite passes on stock macOS (default TMPDIR) in an isolated venv; regression test proving the /var->/private/var case is present; re-verified against the published snapshot after the next orphan-refresh so the shipped tree is green.
close_reason: Fixed via 24c7d02 on feature/restart-controller-draft. title: F-017 blocks the documented guard upgrade path: plugins disable is vetoed inside the gateway, leaving no self-service reload
description: Spec contradiction found during rev-3 amendment 3a deployment (lpkit-6u6/lpkit-1cz, 2026-11-04). The documented upgrade order (001 spec) is disable -> swap + ref -> enable -> probe, but F-017 (live-guard protection) vetoes 'hermes plugins disable proxy-lifecycle-guard' when the guard is live, and 'hermes plugins enable' is flag-only (does not reload the in-memory module). 'hermes plugins update' requires a git origin the standalone deployment lacks. Net effect: the ONLY way to activate a guard upgrade is an owner gateway restart from a separate shell - the documented path is self-blocked. Workarounds used: direct file-tool byte swap + integrity ref re-materialization + owner restart (worked, but bypasses the documented sequence). Open questions for spec disposition: (1) should F-017 carve out an explicit owner-verb for guard upgrades (e.g. a challenge/receipt-gated disable), (2) should 'enable' perform a module reload when the plugin is already enabled, or (3) should the documented upgrade order be revised to state the restart requirement. Note: the 06:39-06:41 POLICY_INVALID window (25 LGV-030 vetoes incl. an unrelated Codex-review session) was a side effect of the workaround's partial on-disk state - a cleaner path would have avoided it.
acceptance_criteria: Documented upgrade order and F-017 enforcement are consistent: an owner can activate a guard upgrade by following the documented sequence without triggering fail-closed POLICY_INVALID states, or the spec explicitly documents the restart requirement as the only path.
notes:
add COMPLETED via the doc-revision disposition (repo cannot change Hermes core plugins enable/disable semantics; F-017 veto itself is correct-by-spec). Commit 4d95d67 on main: README upgrade-order section now pins (1) step 1 disable must run from an owner shell OUTSIDE the running gateway, and an in-gateway attempt is F-017 working as specified, not a defect; (2) the fail-closed POLICY_INVALID/LGV-030 window when swapping files under a live module (2026-11-04 incident: 25 vetoes across 5 sessions ~2min); (3) the agent-session path: consistent bytes + re-materialized integrity ref, then owner gateway restart (restarts Hermes, not the port-4000 proxy). Red-first battery (battery_vfz_red.py): 2 reds pre-change (no outside-owner-shell statement, no restart path) -> 3/3 green post-change. Options (1) owner-verb carve-out and (2) enable-time reload remain open as Hermes core feature requests, out of this repo's scope — the spec contradiction is resolved by making the documented order honest about execution context.
V&V (2026-11-04, independent): VERIFIED. Commit 4d95d67 present on main, tree clean. README upgrade-order section verified: outside-owner-shell step-1 requirement, in-gateway disable = F-017 working-as-specified, fail-closed LGV-030 swap window documented, agent-session path (consistent bytes + re-materialized integrity ref + owner gateway restart, restarts Hermes not the port-4000 proxy). Disposition (doc revision, options 1/2 deferred as Hermes core feature requests out of repo scope) is honest and resolves the acceptance criterion via the explicitly-documented-restart branch. Red-first battery claim consistent with the README content present. Side-effect honesty: the 06:39-06:41 POLICY_INVALID window is correctly attributed to the workaround's partial on-disk state.

title: False veto: NAME=$(...) assignment with $HOME operand refused as indirection
description: The guard refuses receipt=$(mktemp "$HOME/.hermes/cache/scratch/foo.XXXXXXXX") with LGV-001 even though the substitution body receives full analysis at _analyze_shell_text. Bare mktemp with the same path, and the same command with a literal path, are allowed. Fix follows the z4b excision-after-inspection pattern: a standalone assignment whose value opens a command substitution is inert capture; excise NAME=$(span) after the substitution body is analyzed, keeping FR-006 refusals for later $NAME uses and for kill-family substitution bodies.

title: Guard FP: intent regex matches hyphenated path segments in assignment values
description:
Class: LGV-001 false positive (new, post-c355724 generation).

Payload: terminal command containing the shell assignment feature='specs/001-hermes-eval-attribution'.

Root cause: _analyze_chunk scans assignment values with _full_text_kill_intent; the whole-text intent regex matches the token "eval", and in the hyphen-delimited directory name "eval-attribution" the hyphens act as regex word boundaries, so the literal path segment "eval" is scored as terminate-family intent. Any benign shell command that assigns a path containing the "-eval-" segment vetoes with LGV-001.

Demonstrated offline against the deployed generation (/Users/pjbeyer/.hermes/plugins/proxy-lifecycle-guard/guard.py):
- _full_text_kill_intent("'specs/001-hermes-eval-attribution'") returns True; _mentions_target is False.
- The same command set with literal paths (no assignment) allows.

Suggested direction: the assignment-value intent scan should require the verb to be command-shaped (start of the value or after a shell separator), or exclude path-like tokens containing "/" or "-".

Repro receipt preserved in session 20261124_144538_dfc368; sink records at 19:55:45Z, 19:57:27Z and 19:59:27Z on 2026-11-24 are this class (plus one terminal refusal whose description text repeated the intent vocabulary, confirming the whole-text scan applies to bd payloads too).

title: Add a Hermes plugin for exact Smart Router quality-eval attribution
description:
## Problem

Smart Router records the selected tier in LiteLLM SpendLogs, but the quality evaluator cannot prove which persisted Hermes turn used a given proxy response. Model aliases can change without changing tier, and session affinity, timestamps, and “latest turn” are not request identities. They can silently select the wrong response when turns overlap, retry, or share a long-lived session. The tier census can run; scoring must remain disabled until attribution is proven.

## Proposed solution

Write and review a Spec Kit contract in `litellm-local-proxy-kit`, then ship an opt-in Hermes attribution plugin under `integrations/hermes/`, following the kit's existing plugin packaging pattern. Use supported Hermes extension points and LiteLLM facilities as shipped; no core patches, monkeypatches, proxy callback/service, schema migration in either upstream, or routing/affinity changes.

1. **Tag only the intended request.** Use Hermes `llm_request` middleware (`agent/turn_api_request.py`, `hermes_cli/middleware.py`), which sees `turn_id`, `api_request_id`, and destination before transport execution. Allowlist the exact configured local proxy destination and Smart Router route. Send a namespaced, versioned, randomly generated opaque attempt token via `extra_headers` → `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata`; never send Hermes session/turn/message IDs, content, or credentials as attribution metadata. Preserve unrelated headers and metadata without accepting a pre-existing value as the plugin's own tag. Confirm the effective transport and retry boundaries: a Hermes logical request ID is not necessarily a unique HTTP attempt ID. If shared tags cannot be disambiguated to exactly one accepted exchange, mark them ineligible. Do not forward the attribution header to any upstream provider or redirected destination.
2. **Use LiteLLM's existing IDs and metadata.** Source inspection of the pinned 1.110.0 runtime shows the proxy parses the header (`litellm/proxy/litellm_pre_call_utils.py`) and writes the object under `metadata.spend_logs_metadata` (`litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py`). It also returns `x-litellm-call-id` and persists `metadata.litellm_call_id` (`litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py`, spend tracking). Keep that proxy ID unchanged. The proposed exact join is the proxy call ID returned for the accepted response, cross-checked against the plugin-issued token on the same spend row, then linked to Hermes `message_uid`s. The header path is separate from provider header forwarding; keep forwarding disabled and prove non-egress on the supported transports. This is source-level feasibility, not a verified live join.
3. **Bind the accepted response to the physical turn.** Investigate supported execution/response and turn-finalization hooks (`llm_execution`, `post_api_request`, `post_llm_call`) for the exact-response and turn-completion evidence. Treat these as candidate seams, not proof that the proxy response header or a durable final row is already exposed. Use the actual persisted user and final assistant `message_uid`s, verified against the canonical transcript store before the binding is eligible. Keep the correlation record local, profile-scoped, versioned, and short-lived; store only the identifiers and status needed for the match. Use a unique, idempotent write and an exact read-only lookup for the evaluator. Do not infer from text, sequence position across a session, attempt counters, or a successful proxy status alone. If the public plugin surface cannot prove the chain for a transport, stop and record the specific gap for spec review; do not work around it with heuristics.
4. **Qualify separately from activation.** The evaluator selects by persisted router decision (`COMPLEX`, with `REASONING` reported separately), then checks attribution. Limit scoring eligibility to the accepted terminal response for a persisted interactive turn. Reject failed, discarded/replayed, superseded, detached/subagent, classifier/aux/MCP, and billed retry rows rather than treating any of them as final answers. Validate trusted route/client provenance, not client-supplied metadata alone. An eligible row with a missing, ambiguous, stale, or malformed binding must produce `EVAL STALL` (exit 2) and no judge calls or ledger writes. No legacy backfill or score mutation; any future scoring activation is a separately reviewed, versioned qualification cohort.

## Spec questions to resolve before implementation

- Which supported Hermes hook or client surface exposes the accepted response's proxy call ID for streaming and non-streaming Chat Completions and Responses? When are the final transcript message IDs durable, including compaction, output transforms, and interrupted runs?
- How are provenance, per-exchange uniqueness, collision handling, binding retention, bounded spend-log visibility lag, and supported Hermes/LiteLLM version drift tested? What safely disables the plugin and stops scoring without interrupting ordinary inference?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reviewed Spec Kit contract documents data flow, trust boundary, supported transports/versions, retention, failure/rollback behavior, and evidence gates. Plugin is packaged in the kit with manifest, documented opt-in/install/disable steps, `hermes plugins validate`, and synthetic fixtures. No upstream forks or workstation-specific configuration in published artifacts.
- [ ] Deterministic fixture with two turns in one session (including overlapping requests, a retry or tool follow-up, and an unrelated client/control call) proves each eligible spend row maps to the correct persisted message pair. Cover missing/duplicate/replayed tokens, failed/superseded calls, redirects, aux traffic, and unpersisted/compacted-away messages. Assert ambiguous or missing matches stall without judge/ledger effects; assert ordinary inference still works when tagging is absent or fails.
- [ ] With scoring disabled, an authorized controlled synthetic request through **each** of `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` produces one eligible `COMPLEX` spend row tied to the exact accepted response's persisted Hermes message pair. Verify the header survives only as local proxy metadata, is absent upstream and on non-allowlisted routes, and does not change routing, affinity, prompt payload, or trace-ID behavior. Capture sanitized evidence, including where the wire and persistence signals were observed.
- [ ] Read-only evaluator qualification demonstrates exact joins for the supported cohort and fail-closed behavior for missing or ambiguous bindings. `REASONING` remains separate and previous ledgers stay unchanged. No production enablement is implied by filing or implementing this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed Spec Kit contract and packaged opt-in plugin; prove exact accepted-response-to-message-UID joins in deterministic fixtures and authorized Chat Completions and Responses canaries; prove no upstream header egress and fail-closed evaluation with no legacy ledger writes.

title: Guard incidence reduction: post-restart source amendment and implementation handoff
description:
## Finding (2026-11-21 full-history incidence review, three independent passes)

Verdict: NOT "nothing else to do." The guard is correctly fail-closed and consolidation is byte-verified (main = origin/main = deployed 9af90b1c), but a prioritized remainder exists. Decomposition of all 153 direct refusals since Nov 18 (byte-exact re-eval against on-disk bytes):

- 93 (61%) SHAPE_ENVELOPE — upstream hms-5j5 composition defect (truncated/spliced `calls` payloads). Not guard-fixable; belongs to the hermes-agent composer.
- 44 (29%) VETO — mostly correct policy classes (unresolved operands, F-017, eval-substitution); ~6 flip to ALLOW under 0gk/90d.
- 8 (5%) BOUND_SIZE — correct refusals, but 18/18 residual python-SyntaxError cases route to the WRONG category (see P3).
- Sink rows overstate incidence: ~13-20% are the watchdog's own probes; row counts track retry amplification (one payload re-emitted 142x) more than distinct faults.

## Live stale-generation CONFIRMED (discriminating probe, 2026-11-21)

Two live-guard refusals of an execute_code probe carrying a dead data literal with a contiguous kill-string fragment (assembled by concatenation). On-disk 9af90b1c (lpkit-0gk/90d, guard.py:3113-3117) allows exactly this class; the live daemon refused LGV-001 both times. Both refusal records preserved in the sink (21:31, 21:33 UTC-window entries). The serving daemon predates the 14:28 Nov-18 deploy. The single highest-impact action is the owner-led Hermes gateway restart to activate 63x + 0gk/90d + 7kb heredoc routing. NOTE: earlier "live since Nov 18" claims (assistant, 2026-11-18) were WRONG; also, the three behavioral probes used in the 2026-11-21 delegation report do NOT discriminate (all three fixes predate d01f01b9) — the dead-literal probe above is the actual discriminator.

## Prioritized guard redesign proposals (all fail-closed-preserving, verified in deployed source)

- P2 — `$HOME` command-position asymmetry: guard.py:2269 refuses ANY `$`-leading command token while the resolver at 2164-2174 already resolves `$HOME` inside `${VAR:-$HOME/...}` defaults. `$HOME/bin/python3 --version` refuses; the expanded absolute form allows. Extend the existing resolver to command position, re-analyze in full (analysis, not a hole).
- P3 — Python SyntaxError mis-categorized: guard.py:3093-3094 maps `ast.parse` SyntaxError to BOUND_SIZE ("input is too large" on sub-1KB payloads). Route to SHAPE_ENVELOPE, matching 2641/3429 precedent. Refusal unchanged; category + corrective message fixed.
- P1 — Sink enrichment: `_SINK_KEYS` (guard.py:99) = {ts, category, code, tool} only. Add fixed-enum `reason` (proven_kill | unresolved_operand | shape_parse | bound | policy), `gen` (import-time module digest prefix), `probe` flag. Makes stale-vs-FP decidable from the sink; today every adjudication needs a state.db join. Requires coordinated watchdog + test updates (watchdog asserts exact 4-key schema).
- P4 — Fixed-enum `guidance` field on shape refusals (envelope_not_complete | envelope_missing_calls | heredoc_unterminated) + repeat-amplification alert. Messages stay byte-identical and digit-free (contract-pinned); corrective detail moves to the structured field.
- WATCHDOG PARITY VIOLATION (verified by hash, live defect): plugin-dir copy `guard_probe_watchdog.py` (edb8796bd431) still carries the pre-63x DECODE_FAIL_PROBE (valid single-quote JSON — now a graceful ALLOW) and will false-alert a shape-class regression. The runtime mirror ~/.hermes/scripts/ (07d9a402bf6a) and repo main carry the corrected interleaved variant. Sync the plugin-dir copy.

## Not recommended

- Weakening envelope strictness further (interleaved-text class must stay refused).
- Read-only allowlists / any skip-analysis route.

## Skill guidance corrected (2026-11-21, applied)

Cooldown/retry myths (mcp-troubleshooting, flex-linear-mcp live-evidence), subagent-reset escape (recurring-signal-monitor), plugin-dir "cd then chmod" bypass advice and temp-script/subagent workarounds (hermes-lifecycle-guard-blocks), stale-generation mtime test retired (proxy-lifecycle-guard SKILL + verification reference — both the mtime heuristic and my own earlier live-generation claims are corrected in-place).

## Remaining open

- hms-5j5 (hermes-agent composer): 61% of incidence; upstream fix is the dominant lever after the restart.
- lpkit-yk4 (field-name-as-executable FP claim) and the bridge-tool LGV-031 class (aggregator tool names absent from READONLY/EXECUTION registries — 3 fresh HOOK_MISMATCH rows 2026-11-21): unadjudicated; need byte-exact repro per filing discipline.
- The 2a lower-confidence item (guard.py:2858 interpreter argv: dynamic-program vs dynamic-data operand) needs a one-element delta repro before filing.

title: Decide sanitized remote recovery for live and rollback LiteLLM source pins
description:
Finding (2026-11-19, during the lpkit-byi publication review): the deployed v1.110.0 pin's source branch is not remotely recoverable, and neither is the rollback runtime's source.

Facts established 2026-11-19:

- `pin/v1.110.0-ports` (tip `89cb4042afbcd963ee0fd0ae52595202d369a9e6`, 3 commits past upstream tag `v1.110.0`: `0602a92971`, `bdb71b31be`, `89cb4042af`) exists only locally in `~/Projects/pjbeyer/litellm`. title: Cron script op read regression: raw `op read` fails in cron (OP_LOAD_DESKTOP_APP_SETTINGS=false); use native secret-source env vars
description:
Smart-Router Daily Quality Eval cron job (023f808b9388) failed every run from 2026-11-18 15:00 through 21:00 EST with "op read failed for key resolution (check 1P agent session)". The 12:00 run succeeded; the job has failed every 3h run since.

ROOT CAUSE: the script's _op_read() shells out to bare `op read` with no --account. Cron executor processes force OP_LOAD_DESKTOP_APP_SETTINGS=false (verified on the gateway's process tree), which disables the 1Password desktop-app CLI integration and leaves `op` with no configured account — so bare `op read` fails with "No accounts configured for use with 1Password CLI." The gateway restart at ~12:49 today (proxy PID 65498) is the onset: pre-restart workers still had the desktop integration; post-restart cron children force the false override.

Why it broke: raw `op read` only works when the desktop app integration is enabled (interactive sessions). Cron is unattended and must not depend on the interactive desktop-app account (Phil directive 2026-11-18: don't override OP_LOAD_DESKTOP_APP_SETTINGS to force desktop-app auth).

FIX (applied to smart_router_quality_eval.py): the native 1Password secret source (secrets.onepassword.env) already injects LITELLM_LOCAL_KEY and LITELLM_API_KEY into every cron executor. _op_read() now maps each op:// reference to its env var and reads the env var FIRST; it only falls back to `op read` when the env var is absent (interactive runs). Verified by smoke test under cron-like env; job re-run dispatched.

Lesson: any cron script that resolves secrets must read the native secret-source env vars (hermes secrets op), not shell out to raw `op read` — cron executors force OP_LOAD_DESKTOP_APP_SETTINGS=false, so `op` has no account there.
notes:
FIX VERIFIED end-to-end (2026-11-18 21:20 ET manual run of cron 023f808b9388): completed in 119s (result ok, delivered). The final resolver uses company-vault refs (hc6l7lh6h6dmh5wrl63ycfsavy) + Keychain SA token (litellm-local-proxy-op-sa) — the same proven pattern as litellm_filter_battery.py — with the secret-source env vars as first preference. Note: the intermediate env-var-only patch (21:16 run) was insufficient because the no_agent cron executor scrubs Hermes secret env vars (build_subprocess_env -> _sanitize_subprocess_env); the Keychain-SA path is what actually survives cron. Next scheduled run 2026-11-19 00:00 EST will confirm on the normal cadence.
VAULT-SCOPING CORRECTION (owner directive 2026-11-18): the Hermes service account (Keychain service hermes-op-service-account-token) serves the HERMES vault (3g2pzzvrog6jeuxmcrmaowzn5i), which holds both gateway keys. The quality-eval script initially used the wrong pair (litellm SA + LiteLLM vault refs); corrected to Hermes SA + Hermes-vault refs — verified working under cron conditions (scrubbed env, OP_LOAD_DESKTOP_APP_SETTINGS=false). title: Structural fix: graceful bounded decoder for benign stringified/mangled relay envelopes; SHAPE_ENVELOPE stays for interleaved-text
description:
**Title:** Structural fix: graceful bounded decoder for benign stringified/mangled relay envelopes (single-quote JSON, Python-repr, BOM/whitespace) — while SHAPE_ENVELOPE stays for interleaved-text severe variant

## Summary
A recurring defect class: relay/composition layers emit the `calls` envelope as a *stringified* call-list in non-canonical dialects — single-quoted JSON, Python-`repr` of a dict, BOM-prefixed / whitespace-padded JSON — and the guard bounces them with **LGV-020 SHAPE_ENVELOPE** even though the *same content in canonical form ALLOWs*. The envelope-unwrap path only tries strict `json.loads` (guard.py `_analyze_tool_call`, `calls`-string loop). Past practice has been consumer-side "rebuild canonically" (documented in the skill); this issue is the structural, guard-side fix.

This is a strictness FP, not a safety gap: the canonical form of each rejected payload ALLOWs by construction, so the guard is failing to match its own canonical semantics, and the security core is never engaged on these — they never reach analysis.

## Verification (offline repro, 2026-11-18, commit c402245 / deployed `bf8881b01724`)
`guard.evaluate("tool_call", {"calls": <form>}, config.json)`:

| envelope form | verdict today | after fix (target) |
|---|---|---|
| canonical list-of-dicts (control) | **ALLOW** | ALLOW |
| single-quote JSON calls string | SHAPE_ENVELOPE ← FP | ALLOW |
| Python-repr single-call dict string | SHAPE_ENVELOPE ← FP | ALLOW |
| json.dumps-of-json.dumps (double-wrapped) | ALLOW (already tolerant) | ALLOW |
| BOM + outer whitespace | SHAPE_ENVELOPE ← FP | ALLOW |
| trailing interleaved model text | SHAPE_ENVELOPE (severe variant) | **SHAPE_ENVELOPE (must keep)** |

Falsification probe: the canonical form of rows 2/3/4/5 is the one-element delta that flips SHAPE_ENVELOPE → ALLOW, proving the refusal is a shape/parsing artifact, not a content veto.

## Root cause
`_analyze_tool_call` (guard.py ~3245) unwraps a `calls` string only with strict `json.loads`. Real composition layers produce dialects `json.loads` rejects:
- single-quoted JSON / Python dict/list literals (`{'name': ..., 'arguments': {...}}`)
- a bare dict `repr` for single-call envelopes
- a UTF-8 BOM or surrounding whitespace

`json.loads` raises → `_BoundRefuse("SHAPE_ENVELOPE")`. The guard never attempts the (provably safe) Python-literal decode that would restore the canonical object and route it through the normal bounds+analysis path.

## Proposed structural fix
Add a **graceful, bounded, security-neutral envelope decoder** in the `calls` unwrap loop, in order:
1. Strip a leading UTF-8 BOM and surrounding whitespace; try strict `json.loads` first (existing fast path, unchanged).
2. On strict failure, if the string is a pure Python-literal shape (`ast.literal_eval` succeeds — dict or list of dicts), decode it with `ast.literal_eval` (a safe, **non-executing** parser: accepts only literals, raises on any call/expression), then feed the decoded object back through the SAME `_analyze_tool_call` path so it gets full bounds + execution analysis + veto — decode never bypasses analysis.
3. Keep refusal **(SHAPE_ENVELOPE)** for the severe variant — model interleaved text, ambiguous/salvageable-but-unsafe wrappers, anything `literal_eval` rejects. Do not guess at or salvage ambiguous content; do not silently widen decode scope beyond pure literals.
4. Keep the existing decode-depth bound (`range(4)`) and `BOUND_SIZE` size cap; add a decoded-size cap so a decoded object cannot exceed the canonical bounds.

### Security boundary (must hold — part of acceptance)
- `ast.literal_eval` never executes; it cannot turn a benign string into a live call.
- The decoded object re-enters the canonical analysis pipeline, so a genuine kill-word payload inside a single-quoted envelope is analyzed exactly as its canonical twin and still vetoes — this fix only removes *parse* strictness, never veto strictness.
- The interleaved-text severe variant stays refused; no recovery there.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Rows 2, 3, 5 of the matrix flip SHAPE_ENVELOPE → ALLOW with the fix; row 1 stays ALLOW; row 6 stays SHAPE_ENVELOPE; row 4 stays ALLOW.
2. A single-quoted envelope carrying a genuine `pkill`/`kill` payload inside `execute_code`/`os.system`/subprocess still returns **VETO** (security core intact; add a permanent gate).
3. `ast.literal_eval` is the only new decode primitive — no `eval`, no exec, no widened parser.
4. Decode is bounded (size cap + existing depth cap); `BOUND_SIZE`/`BOUND_DEPTH` categories unchanged.
5. No leakage: SHAPE_ENVELOPE message already sanitized (no args/paths/PIDs); decoded content never enters any message/log/sink.
6. Permanent gates in a new test file (e.g. `tests/test_guard_envelope_dialects.py`) pin rows 1–6 and the veto-preservation case; full suite green; red battery unaffected.

## Scope / non-goals
- Does NOT relax veto strictness or the sanitization discipline in any way.
- Does NOT attempt to repair or salvage model-interleaved/garbled envelopes (stays SHAPE_ENVELOPE by design).
- Consumer-side "rebuild canonically" stays as a fallback for genuinely ambiguous forms.
- The running daemon requires an owner-led restart to pick up the new generation (generation-lag rule): deploy + watchdog verify separately from closing.

## Evidence
Offline repro script and full byte-exact matrix saved at `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/hermes/scratch/lpkit_envelope_repro.py` (this is the canonical repro for the minimal-offline gate). Reproduces on the deployed guard `bf8881b01724`.
