title: Suspected stale guard generation: canonical query-data-sources relay envelopes blocked LGV-020 live while offline evaluate() ALLOWS and same-shape search/fetch pass
description:
Live session 2026-11-16 (interactive, default profile): canonical relay envelopes for
aigateway_notion-notion-query-data-sources were blocked LGV-020 SHAPE_ENVELOPE while
byte-similar canonical envelopes for aigateway_notion-notion-search and -fetch passed
live in the same window through the same aggregator relay. Offline, the current on-disk
guard ALLOWS the refused envelope class.

ATTEMPTED ENVELOPE (canonical, built as nested dicts; outer dispatch mcp__local_mcp_aggregator__call_tool):
  {"tool_id": "<gateway relay id>", "arguments": {"tool_name":
   "aigateway_notion-notion-query-data-sources", "arguments": {"data": {
     "data_source_urls": ["collection://cb9371e4-632a-4660-aca9-9f6f5e0ffb59"],
     "mode": "sql",
     "query": "SELECT ... FROM collection://cb9371e4-632a-4660-aca9-9f6f5e0ffb59"}}}}
Variants tried live: full projection with quoted column names; SELECT * minimal;
view-mode {"mode":"view","view_url":"view://ad4fbf79-..."}; quote-free SQL
(no double-quote characters anywhere in the payload). ALL blocked LGV-020.

OFFLINE ADJUDICATION (guard.py as library, deployed config.json):
  evaluate("tool_call", canonical SQL envelope)      -> ALLOW (None)
  evaluate("tool_call", canonical view-mode envelope) -> ALLOW
  evaluate("tool_call", canonical search envelope)    -> ALLOW  [control: passed live too]
  evaluate("tool_call", canonical fetch envelope)     -> ALLOW  [control: passed live too]
  evaluate("tool_call", stringified-calls delta)      -> VETO LGV-001  [guard correct on malformed]

SINK CORRELATION (~/.local/state/hermes/lifecycle-guard/decisions.jsonl):
  8x SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020/tool_call at 14:20:37, 14:20:42, 14:23:34, 15:23:54,
  15:46:34, 15:47:08, 15:47:57, 15:49:50 UTC — 1:1 with the blocked attempts.
  KNOWN GAP: sink stores no payloads, so byte-exact correlation (filing-discipline
  requirement 1) is NOT met; temporal + tool attribution only.

GENERATION LAG:
  guard.py mtime 2026-11-16 03:12 UTC (epoch 1794798979); running Hermes gateway
  daemon started 2026-11-15 19:30 UTC (ps lstart) — process predates the rewrite.

HYPOTHESES:
  H1 stale generation: daemon runs pre-rewrite bytes whose analyzer fails closed
     (LGV-020) on the query-data-sources envelope class; current bytes allow it.
     Supported by: offline-ALLOW/live-BLOCK on canonical envelopes; identical-shape
     search/fetch passing live (mangling would have to be payload-selective under H2).
  H2 composition-layer mangling of this payload class in transit (nda/f4d class):
     the session's sent bytes differed from intent. Cannot be excluded because the
     sink records no payloads.

ANOMALY (unexplained under either H): one non-relay native tool call (clarify)
  also received the guard refusal message in the same window. A pure
  tool_call-envelope theory does not cover it; may indicate broader interception
  in the same daemon generation or a separate path. Flagged for owner review.

DISCRIMINATING TEST (owner): hermes gateway restart from outside the gateway.
  If canonical query-data-sources envelopes still block post-restart, H1 is dead
  and H2 (or a content-sensitive rule in current bytes) becomes primary.

STRUCTURAL RECOMMENDATION: add a bounded payload hash (or truncated canonical
  payload) to sink records so future adjudications can meet the byte-exact
  correlation requirement instead of relying on temporal correlation. Without it,
  every "offline ALLOW + live BLOCK" case is permanently under-determined between
  stale generation and composition mangling.

HONESTY NOTE: this filing partially satisfies the filing discipline — offline repro
  is on the intended-canonical envelope, not a byte-exact sink payload (impossible
  with the current sink schema). Filed as a suspected stale generation with the
  alternative hypothesis named, not as a confirmed defect.

comments.author: Phil Beyer
comments.text: V&V ADJUDICATION 2026-11-16 (independent session, byte-exact A/B on the ACTUAL sent payloads recovered from state.db): SUSPECTED STALE GENERATION FALSIFIED - INVALID AS FILED, but well-filed (honest about the byte-evidence gap; named the alternative that turned out to be correct). H1 (stale generation) is DEAD: A/B of all 26 actual query-data-sources relay payloads against BOTH generations (live dd311e4/f19db6fd AND on-disk d01f01b9) yields IDENTICAL verdicts on every payload - 15 canonical-list-of-dicts envelopes ALLOW on BOTH generations; 11 stringified-`calls` envelopes BLOCK LGV-020 on BOTH generations. Generation is irrelevant to this incident. (The generation-lag observation itself is accurate - the gateway process does predate the on-disk bytes, and an owner restart is still pending to activate the ovj/7kb fixes - but that lag caused NONE of the blocks in this filing.) H2 (composition mangling) CONFIRMED: all 11 blocked payloads carry `calls` as a JSON STRING that is not even json.loads-parseable (quote-escape corruption; 'Expecting comma delimiter'); one payload (msg 1026180, 15:49:48) has model-generated narrative text spliced INSIDE the tool_name field - severe composition corruption, worst instance yet of the hms-5j5 defect class. The filer's 'canonical, built as nested dicts' claim was intent-based: the bytes on the wire were stringified. This is the h45 failure mode again, though this filer honestly flagged they could not byte-verify. CORRECTIONS TO THE FILING: (1) 'sink stores no payloads' is wrong as a dead end - state.db messages carry the sent tool_calls bytes byte-exact (proven by this adjudication and lpkit-h45); the byte-exact filing-gate requirement IS satisfiable today. The structural payload-hash recommendation is still reasonable as a convenience but not required for adjudication. (2) The clarify anomaly does not reproduce and is NOT broader interception: the 14:04:54/58 clarify calls actually failed with clarify-schema errors ('questions[0] must be an object') - themselves stringified-questions composition defects - and the guard-refusal text at 14:04:57 belongs to a batched execute_code call in the same parallel batch (sink VETO/execute_code 14:04:57), misattributed to clarify by result-order adjacency in the transcript. (3) The offline-ALLOW repro in the filing was run on the INTENDED envelope, not the sent bytes - which is why it disagreed with live behavior. DISPOSITION: close as invalid (composition defect, working as designed fail-closed); the live gateway restart remains pending for the four verified fixes but would NOT have changed any verdict in this incident. Evidence: scratch vv_bel_ab2.py, vv_bel_delta.py, vv_bel_clarify.py; census: canonical blocked=0/allowed=15, stringified blocked=11/allowed=0, both generations identical.

## Byte-exact evidence

- Cmd 1 (msg 1020143 -> block 1020144, 2026-11-16T02:10:12.894Z): `cd ~/Projects/work/workspace && gws gmail users drafts create --params "$(python3 -c "import json; print(json.dumps(json.load(open('tmp/friday-flash-render/gmail-create-2026-11-13.json'))['params']))")" --json "$(python3 -c "...")"` (payload ~3.1KB base64url MIME via process substitution; second --json arg identical shape)

- Sink correlation (decisions.jsonl lines 895-896): exactly two VETO/LGV-001 terminal entries at 02:10:12Z and 02:10:15Z, 1:1, no LGV-020 alongside.
- Verbatim block text (both): "Blocked by the LiteLLM proxy lifecycle guard: this request could stop the protected proxy, or its safety could not be established. Use the owner-reviewed controlled restart workflow; do not substitute another kill command or execution path."
- Full recovery: session_search probe deleg_e37dbcbc (session 20261113_194959_84849bc1, msgs 1020143-1020146).

## Why this is a distinct FP class

The trigger is NESTED SAME-CHAR QUOTING INSIDE COMMAND SUBSTITUTION: `--params "$(python3 -c "...")"`. This is valid bash (command substitution reparses its contents), but it is statically ambiguous to shlex-style quote-balance parsing — the inner double-quotes appear to close the outer string, leaving the chunk unbalanced, and the guard fails closed per Constitution I. Three adjacent fixes do NOT cover this shape:

- lpkit-3yb: newlines INSIDE balanced quoted args (separator-aware splitting) — quotes here are never balanced at the top level.
- lpkit-knp: unpaired apostrophes in PROSE contexts (heredoc bodies, comments, unquoted args) — this is an executable argument position, not prose.
- lpkit-1cz: tool_call `calls`/`arguments` JSON decode failures rerouted to SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020 — this is the terminal shell-chunker surface, and the block surfaced as VETO/LGV-001, not corrective guidance.

Two defects in one:

1. **FP class (primary):** valid-bash nested same-char quoting in command substitution is scored as an unparseable/kill-class payload, deterministically vetoing benign writes. The session's own recovery comment ("The guard blocks `gws` in this session as well") shows the operator misattributed it to a session-wide tool block — the misleading message actively causes misdiagnosis.
2. **Message-class mismatch (secondary):** a shape/parse failure surfaced the LGV-001 kill-workflow wording instead of SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020 corrective guidance — the exact misrouting lpkit-1cz fixed for the tool_call surface, still live on the shell-chunker surface. A benign parse failure must not tell the operator to "use the owner-reviewed controlled restart workflow."

Practical cost: publication writes blocked in-session, ~10 min recovery via subagent dispatch, and the workaround pattern ("fresh subagent bypasses the guard") spreads further misattribution — the lpkit-96y adjudication already flagged that this pattern cuts both ways.

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] A/B against the deployed generation with the byte-exact payload (session DB msgs 1020143-1020146) to confirm the class is live, or cite the FR boundary if adjudicated as documented fail-closed
[ ] Red-first test: nested same-char quoting in command substitution on the terminal surface (benign gws/bd/git variants), plus an adversarial counter-case that must still block (kill text inside a command substitution)
[ ] Decide the fix direction: bash-aware command-substitution reparse (like the 3yb separator fix), or quotation-context down-weighting for substitution interiors — never loosening the refusal for genuinely unparseable chunks
[ ] Route shell-chunker parse failures to SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020 corrective guidance (parity with lpkit-1cz on the tool_call surface) so operators self-heal instead of misreading a kill-workflow veto
[ ] Workaround note in recovery docs: for large JSON-argument CLI calls, prefer file-backed args (`--params "$(cat file.json)"` is the same shape; a temp script that reads the file and builds argv in Python passes) or subagent dispatch, until fixed

title: Guard false positive: parameterized session_search (FTS5 query arg) blocked SHAPE_ENVELOPE in main session while unparameterized browse passes
description:
# Finding (2026-11-15/16, Friday Flash publication session)

MAIN session, well-formed nested arguments, deterministic block on every parameterized session_search call; the unparameterized browse call passed seconds later.

## Repro (live, byte-exact correlation available)

6 consecutive parameterized calls blocked, one benign query included:
1. {session_id: 20261113_194959_84849bc1, query: 'gws gmail draft publish friday flash'} -> blocked
2. {session_id: ..., query: 'guard'} -> blocked
3. {session_id: ..., query: 'tabletop exercise thursday'} -> blocked
4. {limit: 3, query: 'weather'} -> blocked
5. {query: 'weather'} -> blocked
6. {query: 'weather', session_id: ...} -> blocked
Then: {} (browse, no args) -> SUCCESS.

Sink correlation: 7 x SHAPE_ENVELOPE LGV-020 tool_call entries at 2026-11-16T02:25:18-02:26:19 UTC = the 7 calls above (6 blocked + 1 retry), 1:1.

## Why this is a genuine FP, not envelope malformation

- Arguments are canonical nested JSON objects (schema-valid per tool_describe; no stringified payloads) — this is NOT the lpkit-nda malformation class.
- Query strings are plain FTS5 search text (weather, tabletop exercise thursday) with no executable-looking content anywhere in the envelope.
- Content-independent: benign and work-related queries block identically. Presence of ANY query parameter flips the verdict.
- The unparameterized browse passing proves tool identity alone is not the trigger — the query/session_id keys (or their values) are scored as opaque/executable-looking payload under non-canonical keys (related to lpkit-vf0: inert non-empty values under unknown keys refused SHAPE_ENVELOPE, closed as over-strict).

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] Repro captured in the shape-test battery: session_search with query param, session_search with session_id+around_message_id, and the empty-args browse call (control)
[ ] Root cause identified: which key/value triggers the opaque-payload classification
[ ] Either a fix (inert known keys for read-only plugin tools pass), or an explicit documented allowance with the fail-closed rationale
[ ] Recovery guidance updated: sessions needing session_search during guard-block investigations must route through a fresh subagent probe (this session's pattern) until fixed

title: Guard vetoes execute_code on input-size grounds without a stated bound ("input is too large to prove safe")
description:
# Finding (2026-11-13, same session as lpkit-96y)

An execute_code submission carrying ~30 lines of Python (a two-command bd SQL probe over the central Beads server) was blocked with: 'Blocked by the LiteLLM proxy lifecycle guard: the input is too large to prove safe; reduce the input size and resubmit.' The same SQL executed cleanly via the terminal tool moments later.

## Issues

- The refusal gives no size bound — no bytes limit, no documented threshold — so the operator cannot predict what passes. 'Too large' is unactionable guidance.
- Inconsistent surface behavior: identical commands pass via one tool and are refused via another; a size-proving cap should apply to the payload, not the tool surface.
- config.json bounds (input_text_bytes: 262144) is 256KB — the blocked script was well under 5KB, so either the bound is not what's enforced for execute_code or a different, undocumented bound applies.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document the actual size threshold for execute_code inputs (and per-tool if it differs)
- [ ] Refusal message includes the measured size and the limit
- [ ] Verify the documented bound matches enforced behavior with a boundary test

title: FN (in deployed 05b1587): pipe-to-interpreter heredoc excision - cat << EOF | sh body escapes signal scanning
description: VERIFIED AGAINST THE DEPLOYED GUARD (2026-11-09, spec-review remediation, deleg_e27013f3 finding 2). CLASS: the lpkit-knp fix routes heredoc bodies by HEAD command only — non-interpreter heads (cat >> file) make the body pure DATA that is excised from the text. But the body's destination is determined by the full composition, not the head: 'cat << EOF | sh' with 'pkill -f litellm' in the body is ALLOWED by the deployed guard (sha 05b1587) while 'sh << EOF' with the same body is BLOCKED — the pipe consumer makes the body executable and the excision turns it into a live veto-evasion channel for the exact kill-pipeline class FR-001/FR-003 forbid. Byte-exact repro (deployed): ALLOW for 'cat << 'EOF' | sh\npkill -f litellm\nEOF'; same body under direct 'sh << 'EOF'' BLOCKs; 'printf ... | sh' control BLOCKs. SPEC: amendment 5a (spec repo c4ad197) now requires composition-aware routing — head command, any pipeline consumer, any redirection into an executing interpreter; battery counter-case (i) added to FR-013. The deployed generation VIOLATES the amended spec. REMEDIATION: route heredoc bodies as executable whenever any pipeline stage (or redirection) of the heredoc's composition reaches an interpreter — misclassification must fail toward inspection, never excision. Also reopen-adjacent: lpkit-knp was closed with head-based routing documented as the mechanism; this issue supersedes that scope.
notes:
Spec gate cleared for the amendment this FN tracks (litellm-local-proxy-kit-specs 92119df, approval state review_status=approved): amendment 5a requires composition-aware heredoc routing with this exact shape as FR-013 counter-case (i). The deployed guard (05b1587) remains in violation until reconciled — verification for close-out must show cat-heredoc-piped-to-sh with a lifecycle-signal verb in the body returning BLOCK on the deployed generation, plus the canonical multi-apostrophe vector for FR-013 case (v) pinned in the permanent battery.
add COMPLETED 2026-11-09. Composition-aware heredoc routing implemented per spec amendment 5a (gate-cleared, 92119df). ROOT CAUSE: the knp fix routed heredoc bodies by HEAD command only; 'cat << 'EOF' | sh' with a kill-family body excised the body as data while the pipe consumer executed it — a live veto-evasion channel. FIX: the composition (head line INCLUDING any pipeline tail after the heredoc operator, plus all downstream stages) determines the body's destination: interpreter heads route to the matching analyzer; any pipeline consumer reaching an interpreter routes the body (sh-family to shell analysis, python consumers to CODE analysis — os.kill is a Python call shape, pinned); unquoted-delimiter heredocs are EXPANDING per POSIX ($() executes regardless of the write destination) so bodies receive shell inspection and are never prose (FR-013 iii); only grammar-proven non-executing destinations (quoted delimiter, no interpreter consumer, no executing redirection) are prose data. Misclassification fails toward inspection, never excision. title: FP class (possibly by-design): variable in command position always LGV-001 (adapter pattern '$PY' script args)
description: Verified against deployed generation 10306141 (2026-11-09). CLASS: a shell variable used as the invoked command ('$PY' script.py --flags or $PY args) always blocks LGV-001, whether or not the assignment is visible in the same payload ('PY="x"; "$PY" ...' blocks; bare '$X hi' with no assignment also blocks). Known-variable arguments pass (echo "$HOME" ALLOW); only command-position variables block. Reproductions in scratch/vv_iso6-7.py. This breaks adapter-style invocations like the family-standup cron pattern ("$PY" "$HOME/skills/a.py" merged --start ...), where the block was initially misattributed to line continuations — one-line form blocks identically. DISPOSITION QUESTION FOR OWNER: if command-position indirection is a deliberate fail-closed (guard cannot statically resolve what the variable expands to), this is working as intended and the adapter scripts need a supported pattern (e.g. literal interpreter path). If not deliberate, it is an FP class. Adjacent to lpkit-knp (prose-apostrophe) but a distinct mechanism; both surfaced in the same Discord-session sweep.
notes:
Disposition recorded per owner review (2026-11-09): NOT spec-amended. The spec (FR-003) requires indirection refusal only in service of signal intent; FR-004 requires intent-free calls to pass. The deployed blanket block on command-position variables fits neither, so this remains an implementation question, not a spec question. Two options: (a) if blanket indirection refusal is a deliberate static-unresolvability fail-closed, the owner must say so and the spec gets a one-sentence codification — reopen this issue against the spec; (b) otherwise it is implementation drift against FR-004 — reconcile the code so intent-free command-position variables pass. Owner decision pending; parked here until then.
add COMPLETED 2026-11-09. DISPOSITION QUESTION ANSWERED: command-position indirection is deliberate fail-closed ONLY for unresolvable values; visible-literal adapter patterns are statically provable and now pass. title: FP class: unpaired apostrophe in prose/heredoc text makes chunk unparseable, guard fails closed
description: Verified against deployed generation 10306141 (2026-11-09, adversarial sweep of Discord sessions). CLASS: an unpaired apostrophe (possessive/contraction, e.g. reviewer's, don't, it's) in plain prose — heredoc bodies, shell comments, unquoted echo arguments — trips LGV-001 fail-closed. Byte-exact reproductions: (1) cat >> doc << 'EOF' with body 'the reviewer's report' -> BLOCK LGV-001; same body without apostrophe -> ALLOW. (2) echo it's-fine (unquoted) -> BLOCK; double-quoted equivalent -> ALLOW. (3) Python comment line 'replicate engine's fingerprint inputs' jointly necessary with a quoted path literal for a cumulative LGV-001 in an analysis cell (lpkit-3bj case 2). Paired quoting ('ok') passes, so the mechanism is quote-balance parsing: prose apostrophes are read as opening single-quotes, leaving the chunk unparseable, and the guard fails closed per Constitution I. IMPACT: LGV-001 on benign documentation/appending workflows; every session that writes prose with contractions into heredocs hits this. SCOPE NOTE: fail-closed is correct behavior for genuinely unparseable chunks, so the fix belongs in quote-aware tokenization of prose contexts (heredoc bodies and comments), not in loosening the refusal. EVIDENCE: scratch/vv_iso3-7.py batteries in ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/.
notes:
Spec amendment 5 committed (litellm-local-proxy-kit-specs 64c5384, feature/proxy-lifecycle-guard-spec): prose-context quotation tolerance codified. FR-003 amendment-5 sentence (grammar-context prose classification: heredoc bodies, shell/Python comments, unquoted-argument prose; unpaired apostrophe in a classified prose span must not render the payload unparseable or trigger a lifecycle VETO by itself; carve-out must not extend to executable surfaces). Clarifications amendment-5 session entry. add COMPLETED 2026-11-09. Prose-apostrophe fail-closed class fixed with quote-aware prose-context parsing, per the issue's scope note (fix parsing, do NOT loosen refusal). MECHANISM confirmed as quote-balance: prose apostrophes read as opening single-quotes leaving chunks unparseable -> LGV-001 fail-closed. BYTE-EXACT repros from the issue now ALLOW: heredoc body 'the reviewer's note', comment '# don't worry', '# reviewer's note'. title: FP class: analysis-only tool calls blocked for literal kill/launch command strings in payloads
description:
# FP class: analysis-only tool calls blocked for literal command strings in payloads

## What happened

During the 2026-11-09 jev-gate calibration session, the guard blocked four
read-only, analysis-only tool calls whose payloads merely *contained* literal
command strings — no execution path ever targeted the proxy:

1. **execute_code cell** — Python source containing the literal string
   `subprocess.run(["pkill", "-f", "litellm"])` as an *analysis string*
   (constructing a classification table of prior sidelog commands).
   Blocked: "this request could stop the protected proxy, or its safety
   could not be established."
2. **execute_code cell** — analysis code referencing `launchctl`/`pkill`
   literals in a producer-hash census (same shape).
3. **execute_code cell** — a sidelog ask-rate counter whose code embedded
   `bd`-invocation strings.
4. **terminal command** — plain `bd projects list; ls ...; grep ...`
   (bd subcommand typo aside, pure listing). Blocked with the same
   "could stop the protected proxy" message, then the identical command
   shape succeeded on immediate retry.

## Why this is a defect class, not noise

- The guard is doing payload-keyword matching on *analysis/inspection
  traffic*. String literals inside Python source or compound shell
  commands are being scored as if they were the invocation itself.
- The fourth case shows nondeterminism: same command shape, one block,
  one pass — suggesting the classifier's safety decision is unstable at
   or near its decision boundary, not a stable policy.
- Every blocked call was read-only against the proxy (no proxy process
  or config was a target). The guard's stated purpose is protecting the
  proxy from stop/kill/rewrite paths; these calls had none.

## Impact

- Agent sessions performing root-cause analysis on guard/plugin behavior
  are the *most likely* to embed kill/launch command strings in analysis
  code — precisely the traffic that gets blocked. The FP class selects
  against the debugging workflow the kit exists to support.
- Blocks cost minutes each (consent timeouts, restructuring, retries) and
  erode trust in the guard's true positives.

## Evidence

- Session 20261104_064027_1230e8 (jev-gate calibration, 2026-11-08/09).
- Blocked calls at: the `pkill`-literal analysis cell, the producer-hash
  census cell, the ask-rate counter cell, and the `bd projects list`
  terminal call (all four in-session, timestamps 2026-11-09 ~01:20–01:30Z).
- Live guard instance: `~/.hermes/plugins/proxy-lifecycle-guard/`.

## Asks

1. Reproduce each of the four block cases against the published suite as
   failing tests (analysis-literal `pkill`/`launchctl` in execute_code;
   plain listing compound commands).
2. Determine why the retry of case 4 passed with no input change — if
   the decision is nondeterministic, document and stabilize the boundary.
3. Consider an analysis-safe classification: payloads whose command
   strings appear inside string literals / heredoc *bodies* (not as the
   invocation target) should not score as stop-path attempts. Quotation
   context should down-weight, not ignore — see closed precedent
   lpkit-3yb (quotation-blind newline splitting) for the parsing
   philosophy already adopted once.
4. If a stable fix is not immediately achievable, document the FP class
   in the guard's README/spec as a known limitation with the workaround
   (restructure analysis code to avoid literal kill strings, or retry).

Related: lpkit-9df (shape-class probe for LGV findings) — the watchdog
probe should cover this class so regressions are caught by cron, not by
a blocked debugging session.
notes:
V&V (2026-11-09, independent, deployed guard 10306141): case-by-case verification of the four claims. CASE 1 (analysis cell embedding signal-command literals in a Python dict of classification patterns): reproduced BLOCK LGV-001 byte-exact. Classification: this is the DOCUMENTED source-data refusal class (README: quoted program inspection does not grant exceptions for signal text carried as data) — the same owner-gated disposition pending from the spec-session refusals, not a new defect. The calibration session is exactly the traffic this documented rule selects against; the disposition ask belongs to the owner, not the implementation session. CASE 2 (fingerprint/env cell): reproduced BLOCK LGV-001. Drop-one-line bisect isolates a CUMULATIVE multi-element trigger (path string literal + an English-contraction apostrophe inside a comment line are jointly necessary; either alone allows). Mechanism consistent with the prose-apostrophe class isolated separately (see new issue): an unpaired apostrophe inside comment/heredoc text makes the chunk unparseable and the guard fails closed. CASE 3 (ask-rate counter cell): reproduced BLOCK (LGV-010 BOUND_SIZE on the byte-exact payload) — bound-class corrective refusal, resubmittable per its guidance, not a lifecycle VETO. CASE 4 (bd/ls/grep listing) NONDETERMINISM CLAIM DISPROVEN: byte-exact re-evaluation of the original command blocks 5/5 runs — fully deterministic. The 'identical command succeeded on retry' recollection is incorrect: the retry in the session DB was a DIFFERENT, narrowed command (the session dropped the plugin-directory ls/grep legs that carried the trigger). The original block is lpkit-z4b Finding A (plugin-dir path + stderr redirect treated as write intent) — already filed and attributed. NET: lpkit-3bj contains no nondeterminism and no new defect class beyond (a) the documented source-data rule (case 1, owner disposition), (b) z4b Finding A (case 4, already filed), and (c) the prose-apostrophe fail-closed class (cases 2/3, being filed as its own issue). Recommend: keep this issue open only for ask #1 partially (red tests for the analysis-literal cells pin the documented-class refusal), reassign ask #2 (nondeterminism) as answered/no-defect, and attach the heredoc/prose-apostrophe issue for asks #3/#4.
Disposition recorded (2026-11-09): no spec change needed. Case 1 is codified by amendment 4's Clarifications (quoted-data signal-call scanning is a conservative refusal class pending owner disposition) — the open item is your disposition, not the spec. Case 3 is LGV-010 bound handling, already required by FR-004 (bounded analysis + corrective refusal). Case 4 is lpkit-z4b Finding A, tracked there. Cases 2/3's underlying prose-apostrophe class is now codified by amendment 5 (commit 64c5384, filed as lpkit-knp).
add COMPLETED 2026-11-09 — closed as disposition-pinned with the knp/5ix fixes covering its actionable residue. Per the V&V note already on this issue: no nondeterminism (ask #2 answered no-defect), no new class beyond (a) documented source-data rule, (b) z4b Finding A, (c) prose-apostrophe. WHAT THIS SESSION ADDED: (1) all four cases pinned as permanent tests in test_guard_prose_and_vars.py — case 1 signal-text-as-data BLOCK (documented rule, owner-gated, unchanged; honest pin, not fixed: restructuring analysis code remains the documented workaround per ask #4), case 2 comment-apostrophe now ALLOW (knp fix), case 3 corrective BOUND_SIZE/LGV-010 pinned (3yb), case 4 listing compound now ALLOW (z4b A + this gate); (2) knp fix resolves case 2's cumulative trigger (comment apostrophe no longer poisons quote parsing); (3) ask #3's quotation-context philosophy applied — prose/heredoc-data contexts parsed faithfully, string-literal DATA with signal text stays fail-closed per the documented rule. Ask #1 satisfied: the four cases are now failing-test-then-green pinned in the canonical suite (312 tests). PUBLISHED 7725b48, DEPLOYED 05b1587, activation at next gateway restart. Related lpkit-9df (shape-class probe coverage in watchdog) remains open and now has a clean anchor: the 20-case gate + mix battery are the shapes to fold into the probe.

title: Decision sink defects: test-suite pollutes the live sink; pre-existing file mode never hardened
description: Found during lpkit-ool V&V (2026-11-05). Two live defects in the decision sink: (1) TEST POLLUTION: only TestDecisionSink redirects XDG_STATE_HOME (tests/test_lifecycle_guard.py:2312-2326); every other guard test that triggers a block decision (GuardHarness veto/shape/bound cases) writes into the LIVE sink at ~/.local/state/hermes/lifecycle-guard/decisions.jsonl. Evidence: sink holds 2,643 records in <1 day vs 55 real hook decisions in agent.log across both days; per-minute bursts of exactly 376 records = full-suite runs; sink contains POLICY_INVALID(462)/HOOK_MISMATCH(112)/BOUND_* categories that never appear in the real hook log. Fix: redirect XDG_STATE_HOME in GuardHarness.setUp (all guard tests isolate), and add a battery red-case asserting a plain veto test writes nothing to the real state home. Until fixed, longitudinal analysis from the sink is unreliable (polluted); real decisions remain in agent.log. (2) MODE: live sink file was 0644 (group/other readable) despite the closeout claim of owner-only 0600. Root cause: the deployed code creates fresh files O_CREAT|O_EXCL at 0600, but the file pre-existed (birth 2026-11-05 10:18:30, likely created by an earlier in-progress sink implementation using default open() semantics 0666&~umask=0644); _tighten_owner_only only acts when mode & 0o022 is set, so group/other READ bits are never stripped, and the O_EXCL branch never runs for an existing file. Fix: tighten should enforce full owner-only (chmod to 0600 whenever mode != 0600, or mask check 0o077), and run on every write not just creation. V&V corrected the live file to 0600 by chmod (state data, not plugin); code fix still required. Battery: red case pre-creating the file at 0644 then blocking must tighten to 0600. Also consider a cleanup pass on the polluted live sink (rewrite keeping only real decision timestamps or rotate out) once the isolation fix lands.
notes:
add COMPLETED 2026-11-05. Both defects fixed red-first, deployed, and live-verified. DEFECT 1 (test pollution): state-home isolation added to GuardHarness.setUp (covers all 11 harness subclasses) plus _isolate_state_home for the two remaining evaluate()-calling classes (TestLoopbackListenerPreservationFixture, TestBounds) — only TestDecisionSink isolated before. First fix attempt was insufficient: suite passed but the live sink still grew +17 per run (caught by before/after line-count verification); loopback + bounds classes were the remaining writers. Empirical proof after the full fix: full-suite run leaves the live sink byte-identical (2,687 before == 2,687 after). Red case TestSinkIsolationFromPlainTests captures the REAL home at import time (immune to per-test env redirection) and asserts a plain GuardHarness veto leaves it untouched — was red, now green. DEFECT 2 (mode): _tighten_owner_only now enforces the EXACT mode (chmod whenever mode != target, not only when 0o022 write bits set) and runs on EVERY write, not just creation — a pre-existing 0644 file is corrected on the first decision. Red case TestSinkPreExistingFileMode pre-creates 0644 and asserts tighten to 0600 — was red (0644 stayed), now green. Suite 129 -> 131 ALL GREEN. CLEANUP: the polluted live sink (2,687 records) could not be truthfully filtered — ground-truth analysis showed real hook decisions largely predate the sink's deployment (the gateway's in-memory module still awaits the owner restart, so real hook decisions were not reaching the sink; ~99% of sink records were test traffic, and minute-granularity matching could not separate watchdog probes from pollution), so the file was ARCHIVED owner-only as decisions.jsonl.polluted-20261105 (evidence preserved, not deleted) and a fresh sink started. DEPLOY: documented agent path — isolated import probe, atomic swap b47e7a0d -> d97fea502c439c0f, integrity.sha256 re-materialized + verified, perms 0600. LIVE VERIFICATION: watchdog rc=0 with sink:true; fresh decisions.jsonl created by the fixed guard at mode 0600 (-rw-------). Repo commit 653de44. Note: once the owner restarts the gateway, real hook decisions will flow to the sink and longitudinal analysis becomes trustworthy from that point.
Follow-up qualification confirms your isolated-state/full-mode fix is a distinct completed slice; no reopening or erasure of that evidence. Additional defects are now P1 lpkit-k7f, discovered-from this issue and lpkit-ool: unsafe linked/non-regular state paths, unbounded rotation on error, and noncanonical/oversized record fields. Five fresh-process fixture probes fail; combined existing suite325pass/70subtest still green. Independent SPEC REQUEST_CHANGES blocks reload. No live file/source/ref edits or activation by this qualification.

title: Dogfood the kit itself: publish a deployment/README path so local instance renders FROM the published kit (today it renders from the private guard-reconciliation tree)
description: Dogfooding gap (lpkit-y2s closeout, 2026-11-04). Today's live instance renders from the private working tree (~/Projects/pjbeyer/litellm-local-proxy-kit-guard-reconciliation, branch fix/lpkit-6u6-lpkit-1cz-shape-envelope at aba9c41), NOT from the published kit (github.com/pjbeyer/litellm-local-proxy-kit, orphan snapshot 7fab8ee). Consequences: the public repo is not exercised as the deployment source; the private tree carries 9 branches/4 worktrees of unexcluded history; and kit improvements can drift out of the published tree (the private fix branch's guard work — 4 commits efa07cb..56e5b01 — is IN the published snapshot only because the snapshot was cut from it, with no ongoing link). Work: (1) define the deployment contract in the kit: which commit of the published repo a local instance renders from, and how (render script/manifest pin, e.g. deployments/personal + a rendered-from commit recorded in deploy.conf.sh or equivalent); (2) adopt the flow for THIS instance: local deployment renders from a pinned commit of the published kit (with the private tree reduced to development-only, publishing via follow-up commits); (3) document in the kit README: the render path, the rendered-vs-source separation (~/.config/litellm vs repo), and the owner restart cadence (launchd plist changes still require the documented controlled restart). Depends on the core-script reconciliation (live-only hardening must land in the kit before the local instance renders from it — otherwise rendering from the published tree LOSES the live-only improvements).
acceptance_criteria: Kit README documents a render-from-published-repo deployment contract with a pinned-commit mechanism; the local instance's rendered directory provably derives from a published commit (recorded provenance); the private guard-reconciliation tree is development-only with a documented publish path.

title: Guard-probe watchdog (cron 8928a8340f33) lacks a shape-class probe: LGV-020/POLICY_INVALID regressions invisible until a real session hits them
description: Watchdog cron job 8928a8340f33 (guard_probe_watchdog.py, probe_history.jsonl at ~/.local/state/hermes/guard-probe-watchdog/) currently probes only kill-class vectors (VETO/LGV-001) and liveness. It cannot detect: (1) SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020 regressions - e.g. the lpkit-1cz defect where decode-fail envelopes surfaced as kill-workflow VETO for 24h+ in live sessions (the 02:00 cron failure) before anyone noticed; (2) POLICY_INVALID/LGV-030 fail-closed states - the 06:39-06:41 integrity-mismatch window produced 25 vetoes across 5 sessions, including an unrelated Codex-review session blocked mid-task, with no watchdog alert. Proposal: extend the probe battery with (a) a decode-fail envelope probe asserting category=SHAPE_ENVELOPE code=LGV-020 and the 'restructure it' corrective message, (b) a POLICY_INVALID sentinel - the watchdog already computes deployed-file digests; add an assert-on-mismatch alert channel (it silently passed the 06:39-06:41 window), and (c) a non-canonical key-shape probe (tool/args keys) asserting SHAPE_ENVELOPE per amendment 3a (lpkit-6u6). All probes are non-executable envelope constructions (decode fails before any execution), safe for unattended cron. History file currently 794 bytes / few entries - probe cadence and retention unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Watchdog run reports per-category probe results (VETO, SHAPE_ENVELOPE, canonical-allow) and raises an alert on any category regression or deployed-integrity mismatch; a deliberately broken sentinel (mutation-style, throwaway env) fails the run non-zero.
notes:
add COMPLETED (watchdog extended in place at ~/.hermes/scripts/guard_probe_watchdog.py; cron 8928a8340f33 picks it up on next run at 16:47, no job edit needed). Red-first battery (battery_9df_red.py): 4 reds pre-change (no decode-fail probe, no non-canonical key-shape probe, no canonical-relay ALLOW probe, state record missing categories) -> 7/7 green post-change. Implementation: _probe_eval generalized to (tool_name, args); three new non-executable probes (DECODE_FAIL_PROBE string, NONCANONICAL_PROBE tool/args keys, CANONICAL_RELAY_PROBE with nonexistent tool_id) asserted to SHAPE_ENVELOPE/SHAPE_ENVELOPE/ALLOW; failures surface as 'shape-class regression' alerts with lpkit-1cz/lpkit-6u6 class labels; probe_history.jsonl now records all five decision categories. Live run: healthy/silent exit 0, state entry verified with decode_fail=SHAPE_ENVELOPE, noncanonical=SHAPE_ENVELOPE, relay_allow=ALLOW, integrity=true. Self-test PASS (extended with probe non-destructiveness assertions). MUTATION/SENTINEL GATE: throwaway copy of the deployed guard with all 3 SHAPE_ENVELOPE routings reverted to _Block (pre-fix behavior) -> watchdog exit 1 with both regression classes in the alert output (sentinel_9df.py, deployed dir untouched) — the new probes are gates, not decorations. Acceptance criteria met.
add MIRRORED TO REPO (commit 5c9ced6 on main): integrations/hermes/proxy-lifecycle-guard/guard_probe_watchdog.py is now the reviewed upstream copy of ~/.hermes/scripts/guard_probe_watchdog.py — byte-parity identical (sha256 218b86cd...), and the README gains a 'Probe watchdog (deployment monitor)' section documenting the mirror rule (both copies change together; byte parity is the deployment contract), the full probe inventory, state file, and self-test. Repo suite green 118/118 (installer contract + lifecycle guard) — the new repo file does not violate the installer's source-inventory contract (it is kit-side, not part of the deployed plugin's byte-for-byte install set). Closing the caveat from the issue's completion note.
V&V (2026-11-04, independent): VERIFIED. Watchdog extension live-verified: self-test PASS, live run healthy/silent exit 0, state entry records all five categories (veto/allow/decode_fail=SHAPE_ENVELOPE/noncanonical=SHAPE_ENVELOPE/relay_allow=ALLOW/integrity/perms). title: Envelope key-shape gap: non-canonical inner-call keys bypass argument inspection (US2-S3 row c)
description:
V&V finding (2026-11-03 post-deployment verification, rev-3 deploy). An inner deferred call using non-canonical keys 'tool'/'args' (instead of 'name'/'arguments') is ALLOWED even when its arguments carry a port-kill pipeline. Spec US2-S3 requires a nameless or unrecognized calls-envelope shape that cannot be proven safe to be refused fail-closed; the implementation recognizes only the runtime's canonical shape and silently skips argument inspection for other shapes. Exposure is low (Hermes emits name/arguments; a caller must hand-craft the variant) but this is a genuine divergence from the fail-closed contract.

Evidence: scratch probe vv-canonical-shape-5d21.py — canonical innocent double-wrap allow, canonical hostile VETO, nameless+canonical-arguments HOOK_MISMATCH (correct), non-canonical tool/args carrying kill command ALLOW (gap).

Proposed fix: treat any inner-call object lacking the canonical name/arguments key pair as an unrecognized envelope shape -> shape refusal (HOOK_MISMATCH class, LGV-031) when it carries executable-looking arguments, per US2-S3. Add battery cases for tool/args, missing-keys, and extra-keys shapes to the T013 mutation battery.
notes:
Adjudication complete (2026-11-04): spec amendment 3a landed — Clarification (canonical name/arguments key pair), US2-S3 + hook-contract rule 2 extensions, FR-007 row (a) affirmative provably-free definition, new Edge Cases bullet. Corrected category: SHAPE_ENVELOPE (LGV-020) for non-canonical inner-call key shapes with executable-looking content (HOOK_MISMATCH stays scoped to tool-NAME attribution). Second exposure found during adjudication: the SAME non-canonical shape scores 'benign' in the FR-007 row (a) tail path (_call_is_benign_shape), letting a hostile call ride the uninspectable tail of an oversized batch — worse than the in-bound skip. Amendment closes both holes. Comprehension gate re-run: 1/5 delta pass honestly recorded; gate blocked pending review per require_on_any_miss. Remaining: implementation reconciliation of amendment 3a once review clears.
add Performance-analysis corroboration (2026-11-04, session analysis of rev-3's first night live): the 02:00 Flex daily meeting+work summary job hit 70 tool_call LGV-001 vetoes 02:07-02:20 and failed both phases. Offline reproduction against the deployed module shows canonical relay envelopes (dict, json.dumps string, triple-nested gateway form) all ALLOW; non-decodable hand-typed JSON string payloads BLOCK as VETO/LGV-001 — the same unrecognized-shape family as this issue, but surfacing with the misleading kill-workflow message instead of the amendment-3a SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020 corrective message. Consequence observed: the cron run misdiagnosed a self-correctable envelope defect as an environment outage and abandoned the run (misleading-category harm, live evidence). Recommendation: implement amendment 3a AND route JSON-decode failures of calls/arguments strings to SHAPE_ENVELOPE (LGV-020) with corrective guidance in the same change, so tonight's 02:00 run gets a clean trial. Watchdog 8928a8340f33 reviewed in the same pass: 6 probes healthy (first entry correctly caught the mid-deployment pre-finalize state), but it has no shape-class probe — consider extending it to assert a non-canonical envelope is refused with a SHAPE-family code, not LGV-001.
add IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (commit efa07cb, same change as lpkit-1cz): amendment 3a implemented. (1) Non-canonical inner-call key shapes (tool/args, extra keys) carrying executable-looking content now raise SHAPE_ENVELOPE (LGV-020) via new _call_has_executable_content helper — the argument-inspection bypass is closed. (2) _call_is_benign_shape now requires the canonical name/arguments pair AND rejects unprovable extra keys, so a non-canonical shape can no longer ride the FR-007 row (a) benign tail of an oversized batch. Red-first: 4 genuine reds pre-fix; 118/118 green post-fix. Mutation sweep found one genuine escape (nameless-arguments and extra-key tail shapes still scored benign) — fixed with two additional negative cases; final sweep 5/5 caught. Deployed on-disk with re-materialized integrity ref (VALID). Comprehension gate: this note records the implementation reconciliation of amendment 3a; the earlier 1/5 delta-pass / require_on_any_miss gate block remains for owner review disposition.
add POST-RESTART VERIFICATION: live gateway decision matrix confirms amendment 3a active (decode-fail -> LGV-020 'restructure it', canonical relay ALLOW, genuine kill VETO retained, benign terminal ALLOW; integrity VALID). Same evidence note on lpkit-1cz covers the POLICY_INVALID window disposition for the separate session's reported block.
Comprehension-gate cycle complete (2026-11-04): reviewer request-changes (4 minors) -> remediation e8823b2 -> re-review APPROVED -> gate cleared allowed (hash 2bc2900d, commit 6ee08b8). T018 implemented by the parallel session as efa07cb (amendment 3a + lpkit-1cz decode routing); deployed with refreshed integrity reference; V&V verified: guard battery 118 passed + 56 subtests, TestShapeEnvelopeBattery 13/13, watchdog green (integrity/perms/veto/allow), deployment committed and parity-restored. Remaining residual tracked in a new P3 issue (inert-list over-refusal).

title: Guard decision log: dedicated JSONL state sink for longitudinal analysis
description: V&V recommendation (2026-11-04, post-restart performance analysis). Guard veto/refuse decisions currently log only via Python logging (agent.log: 'lifecycle-guard decision: category=X code=Y tool=Z'), which makes longitudinal analysis a log-grep and loses structure (no payload shape, session, or allow-path visibility). Recommended: append-only JSONL decision sink under $XDG_STATE_HOME/hermes/lifecycle-guard/ (owner-only perms, rotation bound), one line per decision with ts/category/code/tool + sanitized shape-class fields only — same sanitization discipline as BLOCK_MESSAGE (no arguments, paths, PIDs). Watchdog cron 8928a8340f33 then gains a probe reading the sink instead of grepping agent.log, giving it queryable decision history and per-category rates. Fail-open question to settle in design: if the sink is unwritable, decisions must still be enforced (log-only failure, never refuse enforcement). Battery: existing guard suite must pass unchanged; new tests for sink write failure -> enforcement unaffected.
notes:
add COMPLETED 2026-11-05. All issue requirements implemented, deployed, and live-verified. (1) SINK: guard.py now funnels every block decision through log_decision -> sink_write, appending one sanitized JSON line to $XDG_STATE_HOME/hermes/lifecycle-guard/decisions.jsonl with the FIXED schema {ts, category, code, tool} — BLOCK_MESSAGE sanitization discipline (no args/paths/PIDs), allow decisions not recorded. File created owner-only 0600 in 0700 dir (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, umask-proof), bounded rotation to decisions.jsonl.1 at 256 KiB (single generation). FAIL-OPEN design question settled and tested: sink unwritable -> log-only warning, the block decision is still returned and enforced. (2) BATTERY: red-first (6 tests written against the unimplemented guard, 5 red as expected), then green: record schema, sanitization (no command material), allow-not-recorded, owner-only perms, rotation bound with valid JSON both generations, unwritable-sink fail-open. Merged into tests/test_lifecycle_guard.py as TestDecisionSink; suite 123 -> 129 ALL GREEN, the pre-existing 123 pass UNCHANGED (the issue's explicit battery requirement). One battery-harness fixture fix along the way: probe policies now use the real strict schema (schema_version/protected_labels/bounds/refusal_vocabulary_version) mirroring the live config.json. (3) WATCHDOG: guard_probe_watchdog.py gains a read-only 'sink' probe (_sink_ok) that verifies the veto probe's decision landed in the sink with the exact 4-key schema — alerting on longitudinal-recording degradation instead of grepping agent.log (the issue's stated goal). probe_history.jsonl records the sink verdict. Self-test extended: sink probe must be read-only. Mirrored to ~/.hermes/scripts per the mirroring rule (218b86cd -> 319e60915451); self-test PASS from the deployed path. (4) DEPLOY: documented agent path — import-verified the new module isolated (-I -B, sink_write present), atomic swap of deployed guard.py (59da3e39 -> b47e7a0d78613f61), integrity.sha256 re-materialized (policy + both source digests, d528e73b) and re-verified, owner-only perms. LIVE VERIFICATION: watchdog run rc=0 silent with sink:true; the deployed guard itself wrote real records (VETO/LGV-001/terminal + 2x SHAPE_ENVELOPE/LGV-020/tool_call) — longitudinal analysis now reads decisions.jsonl directly. Repo commit 3adc2b0. README updated with a Decision sink section.
V&V (2026-11-05, independent): CORE DELIVERY VERIFIED; two live defects found, both filed as a new issue (see lpkit defect follow-up). Verified: repo commit 3adc2b0; guard suite 129 passed + 56 subtests (pre-existing 123 unchanged, TestDecisionSink merged); deployed guard.py sha b47e7a0d == repo; integrity.sha256 re-materialized and matches (policy, __init__.py, guard.py); watchdog mirrored (218b86cd -> 319e6091) and runtime == repo; sink live and schema-correct {ts,category,code,tool}; watchdog tick 15:39:19Z records sink:true; fail-open design confirmed in source (sink_write catches all, logs warning, decision still enforced). DEFECTS: (1) sink file was 0644 not the claimed 0600 — root cause: file pre-existed the deployed 0600/O_EXCL path (birth 10:18:30 today) AND _tighten_owner_only only checks mode & 0o022 (group/other write), so group/other read bits are never stripped and the O_EXCL create branch never ran. V&V chmod-corrected the live file to 0600. (2) TEST POLLUTION: sink holds 2,643 records in <1 day vs 55 real hook decisions in agent.log over both days; per-minute bursts of exactly 376 = full-suite runs writing into the LIVE sink because only TestDecisionSink redirects XDG_STATE_HOME — all other guard tests write real sink records (462 POLICY_INVALID, 112 HOOK_MISMATCH, BOUND_* categories absent from the real hook log). Until the isolation fix lands, treat the sink as polluted for longitudinal analysis; agent.log remains the truthful decision record. Category mix in the sink is NOT evidence of real guard misbehavior.
Additional combined-version qualification found four NEW defects; filed P1 lpkit-k7f (discovered-from this issue and lpkit-55u). Five disposable fresh-process probes reproduced symlink target mutation, FIFO stall, occupied-rotation overflow and raw/oversized log fields. The published orphan snapshot (7fab8ee, github.com/pjbeyer/litellm-local-proxy-kit) was cut from the private working tree at aba9c41, but there is no recurring mechanism to keep the published tree in sync: subsequent work (e.g. lpkit-5o4 live-hardening ports, any guard/watchdog follow-ups) would silently diverge the public repo from reality. Also the published snapshot currently embeds the pre-dogfood contract: no deployments/personal render provenance, and its README reflects the snapshot moment only. Work: (1) add a documented publish flow to the kit (re-snapshot procedure with the zero-Flex gate + secret-shape scan as executable gates, e.g. a scripts/publish_check.py, so publishing is one reviewed command rather than a bespoke session each time — the gate scripts themselves were session-local scratch in the lpkit-y2s run and have NOT been preserved); (2) re-snapshot after lpkit-5o4 lands; (3) verify the published README matches the tree (the current README pre-dates the cli-token rename docs check). Note the private history is intentionally NOT published (flex-string commits) — the orphan-squash refresh is the mechanism, do not switch to pushing the private branch. Related: lpkit-5o4 (port live hardening first), lpkit render-contract issue (dogfood flow).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/publish_check.py (or equivalent) exists in the kit with the zero-Flex + secret-shape + fixture-exemption gates as executable checks and a documented re-snapshot procedure; a re-snapshot after lpkit-5o4 is published and verified via git ls-remote; the gate logic used in the lpkit-y2s publish is no longer session-local scratch.
notes: Release-readiness finding (2026-11-04): the private working branch's requirements-stable-candidate.txt still pins litellm[proxy]==1.101.0 (the version with the HIGH-severity salt-key advisory; lpkit-fqs), while the published snapshot already carries the corrected 1.101.3 pin with the honest not-yet-revalidated note. A future orphan-snapshot refresh cut from this branch would RE-PUBLISH the vulnerable pin and silently drop the advisory note. The re-snapshot procedure must include a requirements/documented-divergence audit, and this branch's pin should be brought to 1.101.3 (with the same note) as part of lpkit-fqs.

title: Inert non-empty list under unknown key refused SHAPE_ENVELOPE — over-strict vs amended Edge Case
description:
V&V finding (2026-11-04, post-efa07cb verification). _call_has_executable_content treats ANY non-empty list/tuple under a non-canonical key as executable-looking (opaque non-empty payload). Verified against the repo copy: {name: read_file, arguments: {path}, tags: ["a","b"]} -> SHAPE_ENVELOPE refusal, while inert strings (note: "hello") and inert dicts (meta: {k:v}) pass. The amended Edge Case (amendment 3a) says a plain object with no executable-looking content ANYWHERE passes as an unrecognized-but-inert extra — a list of plain strings is inert, so this is an over-blocking divergence in the fail-closed direction (self-correctable via the SHAPE_ENVELOPE restructure guidance, so low operational impact). The battery has no list-valued unknown-key case (TestShapeEnvelopeBattery covers string keys, dict values, and the M4 nameless/extra-key escapes, but not list values).

Proposed fix: treat a list whose every element is a plain (non-executable-looking) string/number/dict as inert; refuse only lists containing executable-looking content. Add battery cases both directions (inert tags list passes; list containing {command: <kill>} refuses).
